text: The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps shall be so installed that correct adjustment of their orientation can easily be carried out.

Measures fitted to headlamps to prevent discomfort to other road-users in a country where traffic operates on the opposite side of the road to that for which the headlamp was designed shall be achieved automatically or by the vehicle user with the vehicle in the park condition without the need for special tools (other than those provided with the vehicle; this does not apply to dedicated objects that may be added to the exterior of the headlamp).
condition: if headlamps are fitted with measures for use in countries with opposite traffic direction

text: Detailed instructions for the traffic-change measures of the headlamps shall be provided by the vehicle manufacturer with the vehicle.
condition: if headlamps are fitted with measures for use in countries with opposite traffic direction

text: For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The reference axis of side retro-reflectors and of side-marker lamps when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.

The reference axis of all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
condition: light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps

text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the normal condition of use defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.
condition: in the absence of specific instructions

text: Where an AFS is installed, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the AFS in its neutral state.
condition: where an AFS is installed

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface).
condition: lamps constituting a pair, in the absence of specific instructions

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
condition: lamps constituting a pair, in the absence of specific instructions

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
condition: lamps constituting a pair, in the absence of specific instructions

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
condition: lamps constituting a pair, except matched pairs and AFS

text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
condition: lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo

text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
condition: lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo

text: All logos in lamps that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
condition: lamps incorporating a logo

text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical the requirements of paragraph 5.5 for lamps constituting a pair shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
condition: vehicles with asymmetrical external shape

text: Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another only provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
condition: if lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
condition: if lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
condition: when a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with other functions that can be switched ON together
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.
condition: where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.
condition: where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1. (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed such that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis. These requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
condition: single lamp whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts; not a single retro-reflector

text: Single lamps composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors (paragraph 2.4.11.1. (b) or (c)) shall be installed such that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro-reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing those projections, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
condition: single lamp composed of two lamps marked D or two independent retro-reflectors

text: Single lamps consisting of an interdependent lamp system (paragraph 2.4.11.1. (d)) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces included in the same lamp body and/or having a common outer lens shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
condition: two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip

text: The illumination of a band or strip lamp surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.
condition: two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip

text: The light-emitting surface of a band or strip lamp may be constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements only on condition that these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
condition: band or strip lamp with juxtaposed elements

text: The maximum height above the ground of a lamp shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
condition: when geometric visibility angles are reduced based on mounting height

text: For the dipped-beam headlamp, the minimum height in relation to the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis independent of its utilization.

The position of a lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
condition: in the absence of specific instructions

text: Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps.
condition: for side-marker lamps: amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7

text: The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, only provided that any variation is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
condition: if photometric characteristics vary

text: The photometric characteristics of a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b may be varied during a flash only by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6. of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11. of UN Regulation No. [LSD]; this shall not apply when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1.
condition: if sequential activation is used; not when categories 2a/2b operate as emergency stop signal

text: The lamp(s) used for the answer-back signal, which may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or apparent surface, shall operate according to the conditions specified in the general specifications and/or in paragraph 6.27.
Reversing projection may vary only according to the steering wheel angle and/or the speed of the vehicle and/or the proximity to an obstacle.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle (interior lighting devices and reversing projections not taken into account).
condition: lamps emitting red light fitted at the rear

text: White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle (interior lighting devices and reversing projections not taken into account).
condition: lamps emitting white light fitted at the front

text: With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
condition: red lamps other than red rearmost side-marker lamp

text: With the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).
condition: white lamps other than reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings

text: In case of doubt, the requirements of paragraphs 5.10.4.1 and 5.10.4.2 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
condition: in case of doubt

text: The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
condition: except while position lamps are used as parking lamps, side-marker lamps flash with direction indicators, daytime running lamps are switched ON, or the front position lamp function is substituted under 5.12.1 (paragraph 5.11.1)

text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

The electrical connections shall be such that the main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11. are also switched ON.
condition: not applicable to main-beam or dipped-beam headlamps when giving luminous warnings by intermittent or alternate lighting up at short intervals

text: Dipped-beam headlamps, main-beam headlamps and/or front fog lamps may substitute the function of the front position lamps only if their electrical connections are such that in case of failure of any of these lighting devices the front position lamps are automatically switched ON again.
condition: if these lamps substitute the front position lamp function

text: A lamp substituting the front position lamp function shall meet the geometric visibility prescribed for the front position lamps in paragraph 6.9.5.
condition: if these lamps substitute the front position lamp function

text: A lamp substituting the front position lamp function shall meet the minimum photometric values of the front position lamp according to the angles of light distribution.
condition: if these lamps substitute the front position lamp function

text: Appropriate evidence demonstrating compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5.12.1.2. shall be provided in the test reports of the substituting lamp.
condition: if these lamps substitute the front position lamp function

text: Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by this Regulation it may be replaced by an operating tell-tale.
condition: where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed

text: The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.

In the event of any failure affecting the operation of the concealment device(s), concealable lamps shall remain in the position of use, if already in use, or shall be capable of being moved into the position of use without the aid of tools.
condition: failure of the concealment device

text: It shall be possible to move concealable lamps into the position of use and to switch them ON by means of a single control, without excluding the possibility of moving them into the position of use without switching them ON; in the case of grouped main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps, the control is required only to activate the dipped-beam headlamps.
It shall not be possible deliberately, from the driver's seat, to stop the movement of switched ON concealable lamps before they reach the position of use.
If there is a danger of dazzling other road users by the movement of the concealable lamps, they may light up only when they have reached their position of use.
condition: if there is a danger of dazzling by the movement of the lamps

text: When the concealment device has a temperature of -30 °C to +50 °C the concealable headlamps shall be capable of reaching the position of use within three seconds of initial operation of the control.
The colour of the light emitted by the main-beam headlamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the dipped-beam headlamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the front fog lamp shall be white or selective yellow.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the direction-indicator lamp shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the hazard warning signal shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the emergency stop signal shall be amber or red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear-end collision alert signal shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear registration plate lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the front position lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear fog lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the parking lamp shall be white in front, red at the rear, and amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The colour of the light emitted by the side-marker lamp shall be amber; however the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The colour of the light emitted by the end-outline marker lamp shall be white in front and red at the rear.
The colour of the light emitted by the daytime running lamp shall be white.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, triangular shall be red.
The colour of the front retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be identical to incident light (white or colourless retro-reflector).

The colour of the side retro-reflector, non-triangular shall be amber; however the rearmost side retro-reflector can be red if it is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp, the red rearmost side-marker lamp or the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular.
The colour of the light emitted by the cornering lamp shall be white.

The colour of conspicuity marking shall be white to the front; white or yellow to the side; red or yellow to the rear (Contracting Parties may allow white conspicuity markings to the rear in their territories).
The colour of the light emitted by the adaptive front-lighting system (AFS) shall be white.

The colour of the light emitted by the exterior courtesy lamp shall be white and, in addition, in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
The colour of the light emitted by the manoeuvring lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The colour of the reversing projection shall be white.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Any lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
condition: if a lamp is installed on a movable component

text: Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraphs 5.18.1 to 5.18.4 are met.
condition: if installed on movable components

text: Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors installed on movable components shall, at all fixed positions of the movable components, meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
condition: if installed on movable components

text: Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector function on a movable component is obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D", only one of the lamps needs to meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.
condition: if the function is obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D"

text: Where additional lamps for the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
condition: if additional lamps are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position

text: Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector function is obtained by an interdependent lamp system completely mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1 shall be satisfied; additional lamps may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position provided they satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
condition: if the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s)

text: Where the interdependent lamp system (other than direction indicator lamps) is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during device approval shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component(s); the inwards geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if these lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for device approval at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
condition: if the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, except direction indicator lamps

text: For direction indicator lamps obtained by an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during device approval shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), unless additional lamps are switched ON in any fixed open position to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle and these additional lamps satisfy all the position, photometric and colorimetric requirements applicable to the direction indicator lamps installed on the movable component.
condition: if the direction indicator interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component

text: When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
condition: when the movable component is not in a normal position of use

text: When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.
condition: when the movable component is in the normal position(s) of use

text: For dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps on movable components, the return-to-position requirement is considered satisfied if, when the movable components are moved and returned to the normal position 10 times, no value of the angular inclination of these lamps relative to its support, measured after each operation, differs by more than 0.15 per cent from the average of the 10 measured values.
condition: if dipped-beam headlamps or front fog lamps are installed on a movable component

text: If the 0.15 per cent value is exceeded, each limit specified in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1 shall be modified by this excess to decrease the allowed range of inclinations when checking the vehicle according to Annex 6.
condition: if the deviation from the average exceeds 0.15 per cent

text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
condition: in any fixed position of a movable component different from the normal position of use

text: If the 50 per cent hiding limit is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component (alternative to 5.21.2).
condition: if the requirement of 5.21 is not practicable and the apparent surface is more than 50 per cent hidden

text: Alternatively, if the 50 per cent hiding limit is not practicable, a remark in the communication form (item 10.1 of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components.
condition: if the requirement of 5.21 is not practicable and additional lamps per 5.21.1 are not fitted; not applicable to retro-reflectors

text: In that case, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements.
condition: if the requirement of 5.21 is not practicable and additional lamps per 5.21.1 are not fitted; not applicable to retro-reflectors

text: The communication-form remark and user-notice alternative of paragraph 5.21.2 shall not be used for retro-reflectors.
condition: if a retro-reflector is more than 50 per cent hidden by a movable component

text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
condition: except retro-reflectors

text: Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except where used as non-replaceable light sources, shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
condition: if the lamp is approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37 not used as non-replaceable light sources

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement of light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 37.
condition: if lamps with replaceable UN R37 light sources are fitted

text: Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.
condition: if a light source module includes a holder for a UN R37 replaceable light source

text: A temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed only provided that the replacement function in case of failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate and the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.
condition: if a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function is provided

text: During temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.
condition: during a temporary fail-safe replacement

text: Where an AFS is fitted, it shall be considered equivalent to a pair of dipped-beam headlamps and, if it provides main-beam function(s), equivalent to a pair of main-beam headlamps.
condition: where an AFS is fitted

text: Rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control responding simultaneously to the conditions of 5.26.1 and 5.26.2 are allowed only provided that the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
condition: if lamps with variable luminous intensity control are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated

text: For rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.
condition: if a prescribed intensity ratio between two lamps applies

text: Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity of variable intensity lamps is allowed only within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations and in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface.
condition: for environmental conditions

text: Independently from environmental conditions, a decrease of luminous intensity of variable intensity lamps, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m; an intensity decrease already activated may remain active as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h.
condition: for traffic conditions

text: Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity, based on the conditions of paragraphs 5.26.1 and 5.26.2, independently from the other lamps.
condition: for S4 stop lamps and F2 rear fog lamps

text: No sharp variation of luminous intensity of variable intensity lamps shall be observed during transition.
condition: during intensity transitions

text: For vehicles of M and N categories the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service that the electric power supply conditions for main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps, stop lamps, front position lamps and rear position lamps comply with paragraphs 5.27.1 to 5.27.4 when the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category as specified by the applicant.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved.
condition: if the device was approved with special power supply, secondary operating mode or applicant-requested voltage; not for devices excluded by 5.27.3

text: In all other electric power supply conditions, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
condition: supply conditions not covered by 5.27.1; not for devices excluded by 5.27.3

text: The voltage provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 shall not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
A report shall be attached to the approval documentation describing the methods used to demonstrate compliance with the electric power supply provisions and the results obtained.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved are not taken into account.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.
condition: if measurements are taken closer to the lamp

text: If, when the lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
condition: if part of the apparent surface is hidden by vehicle parts

text: When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to paragraph 5.8.1), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
condition: lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground

text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
A LED module does not need to be replaceable only if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 when installed on a vehicle.
condition: where applicable

text: Light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
condition: if the light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: Lamps installed on a vehicle approved to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources unless they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
condition: if lamps are approved for replaceable light source categories

text: One external status indicator for Vehicle Alarm System (VAS), Alarm System (AS) and immobilizer is allowed only if its light intensity in any direction does not exceed 0.5 cd.
condition: if an external status indicator is fitted

text: The colour of the light emitted by the external status indicator shall be white, red or amber.
condition: if an external status indicator is fitted

text: The area of the apparent surface of a single external status indicator shall not be larger than 20 cm2.
condition: if one external status indicator is fitted

text: Up to two external status indicators for VAS, AS and immobiliser are allowed on a vehicle provided that the apparent surface does not exceed 10 cm2 per indicator.
condition: if two external status indicators are fitted

text: A device type approved according to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148, 149 and/or 150 may be fitted on the vehicle to be type approved without update of device approval documents and markings only when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ from those of the latest series of amendments.
condition: if the device is approved to a preceding series of UN R148, R149 or R150

text: The use of lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) is allowed exclusively where the manufacturer's statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8 is present and positive.
condition: if lamps equipped with LED substitute light sources are used

text: At type approval and in conformity of production verification, the presence of the marking on the lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall be checked.
condition: if lamps equipped with LED substitute light sources are used

text: The Driver Assistance Projection shall be constituted of patterns, symbols or both.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: Driver Assistance Projection symbols and patterns shall be related and limited only to warning/highlighting the presence of hazardous traffic situations, the presence of other road users requiring the driver's attention, maintaining the distances to surrounding road users and infrastructure, and maintaining the correct lane.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: The Driver Assistance Projection patterns and symbols shall be explained in the owner's handbook.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: Only the symbols and patterns listed in Annex 16, under their associated underlying conditions, may be used for the Driver Assistance Projection.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: Neither flashing nor transforming of Driver Assistance Projection is permitted, unless expressly allowed for the use cases described under the conditions in Annex 16.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: It shall always be possible to manually deactivate and reactivate the system which operates the Driver Assistance Projection.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: The projected Driver Assistance Projection symbols and patterns shall no longer be projected when their associated underlying conditions allowing them to be shown no longer exist.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: The projected Driver Assistance Projection symbols and patterns shall stop flashing when their associated underlying conditions allowing them to flash no longer exist.
condition: if flashing projection is provided

text: The Driver Assistance Projection shall be deactivated automatically in case of an electrically detectable failure of the system that affects the visual information on the road given by the projection.
condition: in case of an electrically detectable failure

text: The Driver Assistance Projection shall not interfere with information displayed by the Field of Vision Assistant as defined in UN Regulation No. 125.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: The Driver Assistance Projection shall not be switched ON when the windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes.
condition: windshield wiper in continuous operation for at least two minutes

text: Except for the wrong way warning, predicted trajectory and risk of collision warning, Driver Assistance Projection shall not be switched ON when the vehicle speed is below 65 km/h; when already switched ON, it may remain switched ON as long as the vehicle speed remains above 40 km/h.
condition: except wrong way warning, predicted trajectory and risk of collision warning

text: Except for predicted trajectory, the lateral distance from the outer edges of the Driver Assistance Projection with respect to the longitudinal median plane or to the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle shall not be more than 1,250 mm.
condition: except predicted trajectory

text: The predicted trajectory Driver Assistance Projection may be adapted according to the predicted trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle; it shall not be wider than the width of the vehicle including any fitted accessories and trailer if applicable and, in any case, shall not be more than 2,600 mm.
condition: for predicted trajectory projection

text: Compliance with paragraphs 5.35.11 and 5.35.12.1 shall be demonstrated by the manufacturer by calculation or by other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: The reversing projection patterns shall be explained in the owner's handbook.
condition: if reversing projection is provided

text: When reversing projections are provided, only the basic elements listed in Annex 17 shall be used.
condition: if reversing projection is provided

text: The pattern of each reversing projection shall be constituted by one or more basic element(s) of the same type in a line.
condition: if reversing projection is provided

text: The number, size, ratio and spacing between the basic elements in the reversing projection pattern are not restricted, provided that the requirements of paragraph 6.28.5 are met.
condition: if reversing projection is provided

text: When more than one reversing projection is switched ON simultaneously, the projected patterns shall not overlap each other.
condition: when more than one projection is switched ON simultaneously

text: When the windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous operation has occurred for at least two minutes, reversing projection(s) whose luminous intensity exceeds 8.00∙10^3 cd shall either be switched OFF or have their luminous intensity reduced to a value less than or equal to 8.00∙10^3 cd.
condition: windshield wiper in continuous operation for at least two minutes and intensity exceeds 8.00∙10^3 cd

text: Conformity to the windshield wiper intensity reduction requirement shall be verified at the time of the reversing projector type approval and indicated in the related communication form.
The applicant shall provide sufficient evidence that the reversing projection will not negatively affect rear camera system performance as defined in UN Regulation No. 158.
condition: if reversing projection is provided

text: Main-beam headlamps shall be present on motor vehicles (mandatory).
Main-beam headlamps are prohibited on trailers.
The number of main-beam headlamps shall be two, type approved according to Class B of the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
Optionally, one or two additional pair(s) of main-beam headlamps may be fitted, type approved according to Classes A or B or RA of the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
condition: if additional pairs are fitted

text: Main-beam headlamps shall be positioned in length at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.

The visibility of the illuminating surface of the main-beam headlamp, including its visibility in areas which do not appear to be illuminated in the direction of observation considered, shall be ensured within a divergent space defined by generating lines based on the perimeter of the illuminating surface and forming an angle of not less than 5° with the axis of reference of the headlamp, the origin of the angles being the perimeter of the projection of the illuminating surface on a transverse plane tangent to the foremost part of the lens of the headlamp.
Main-beam headlamps shall be oriented towards the front.
Not more than one main-beam headlamp on each side of the vehicle may swivel to produce bend lighting.
condition: if main-beam headlamps swivel to produce bend lighting

text: Except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals, the main-beam headlamps may be switched ON only when the dipped-beam headlamps are manually activated or the conditions for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.
condition: except when used for intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals

text: The main-beam headlamps shall be switched OFF automatically when the dipped-beam headlamps are manually deactivated or the conditions for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps cease to exist.

The control of the main-beam headlamps may be automatic regarding their switching ON and OFF only if the control signals are produced by a sensor system capable of detecting and reacting to each of: (a) ambient lighting conditions; (b) the light emitted by the front lighting devices and front light-signalling devices of oncoming vehicles; (c) the light emitted by the rear light-signalling devices of preceding vehicles, where vehicles means categories L, M, N, O, T and bicycles equipped with retro-reflectors and switched-ON lighting and light-signalling devices.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: It shall always be possible to switch the main-beam headlamps ON and OFF manually and to manually deactivate the automatic control of the main-beam headlamps.
The switching OFF of the main-beam headlamps and the deactivation of their automatic control shall be by means of a simple and immediate manual operation; the use of sub-menus is not allowed.
The main-beam headlamps may be switched ON either simultaneously or in pairs; for changing over from the dipped to the main beam at least one pair of main-beam headlamps shall be switched ON.
condition: when changing over from dipped to main beam

text: For changing over from the main-beam to the dipped-beam all main-beam headlamps shall be switched OFF simultaneously.
condition: when changing over from main beam to dipped beam

text: Auxiliary driving-beam(s), class RA, shall only be switched ON together with the driving-beams of another class, except when one or more pair(s) of class RA auxiliary driving-beams are used to produce light signals consisting of intermittent switching ON at short intervals (paragraph 5.12.).
condition: if class RA auxiliary driving-beams are fitted

text: The dipped-beams may remain switched ON at the same time as the main beams.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the main-beam headlamps is mandatory.

If the control of the main-beam headlamps is automatic as described in paragraph 6.1.7.2., an indication shall be provided to the driver that the automatic control of the main-beam function is activated, and this information shall remain displayed as long as the automatic operation is activated.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The reference value corresponding to the aggregate maximum intensity of the main-beam headlamps which can be switched ON simultaneously shall not exceed 100.
The aggregate maximum intensity of the main-beam headlamps shall be obtained by adding together the individual reference marks indicated on the several headlamps.

The sensor system controlling automatic switching of the main-beam headlamps shall be able to detect light emitted from other vehicles within minimum horizontal angles of 15° to the left and 15° to the right, measured from the centre of the sensor aperture relative to a horizontal straight line through its centre parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The sensor system controlling automatic switching of the main-beam headlamps shall be able to detect light emitted from other vehicles within a minimum upward vertical angle of 5°.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The sensor system controlling automatic switching of the main-beam headlamps shall be able to detect light within a minimum downward vertical angle of 2° when the sensor mounting height (centre of sensor aperture above the ground) is less than 2 m.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic and sensor mounting height is less than 2 m

text: The sensor system controlling automatic switching of the main-beam headlamps shall be able to detect light within a minimum downward vertical angle of 2° to 5° when the sensor mounting height is between 1.5 m and 2.5 m.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic and sensor mounting height is between 1.5 m and 2.5 m

text: The sensor system controlling automatic switching of the main-beam headlamps shall be able to detect light within a minimum downward vertical angle of 5° when the sensor mounting height is greater than 2.0 m.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic and sensor mounting height is greater than 2.0 m

text: The sensor system for automatic main-beam control shall be able to detect on a straight level road an oncoming power driven vehicle at a distance extending to at least 400 m, the oncoming vehicle having position lamps (if applicable) and dipped-beam headlamps switched ON.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The sensor system for automatic main-beam control shall be able to detect on a straight level road a preceding power driven vehicle or a vehicle-trailer combination at a distance extending to at least 100 m, the preceding vehicle having position lamps (if applicable) and dipped-beam headlamps switched ON.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The sensor system for automatic main-beam control shall be able to detect on a straight level road an oncoming bicycle at a distance extending to at least 75 m, its illumination represented by a white lamp with a luminous intensity of 150 cd, a light emitting area of 10 cm² ± 3 cm² and a height above ground of 0.8 m.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The automatic transition from main-beam to dipped-beam and vice versa according to the conditions of paragraph 6.1.7.2. shall not cause discomfort, distraction or glare.
condition: if the transition is performed automatically

text: The overall performance of the automatic main-beam control shall be verified by means of simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Type Approval Authority, as provided by the applicant.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The overall performance of the automatic main-beam control shall be verified by a test drive according to paragraph 1 in Annex 12; the performance shall be documented and checked against the applicant's description, and any obvious malfunctioning (e.g. excessive angular movement or flicker) shall be contested.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: The main-beam headlamps may be switched ON automatically only when no vehicles as mentioned in paragraph 6.1.7.2. are detected within the fields and distances of paragraphs 6.1.9.3.1.1. and 6.1.9.3.1.2., and the detected ambient lighting levels are as prescribed in paragraph 6.1.9.3.5.
condition: if the main-beam control is automatic

text: Where main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically, they shall be switched OFF automatically when oncoming or preceding vehicles, as mentioned in paragraph 6.1.7.2., are detected within the fields and distances of paragraphs 6.1.9.3.1.1. and 6.1.9.3.1.2.
condition: if the main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically

text: Where main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically, they shall be switched OFF automatically when the illuminance produced by ambient lighting conditions exceeds 7000 lx.
condition: if the main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically

text: Compliance with the automatic switch-OFF requirement at ambient illuminance above 7000 lx shall be demonstrated by the applicant using simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Type Approval Authority; if necessary the illuminance shall be measured on a horizontal surface with a cosine corrected sensor at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle, which may be demonstrated by sufficient documentation or other accepted means.
condition: if the main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically

text: Dipped-beam headlamps shall be fitted on motor vehicles (mandatory).
Dipped-beam headlamps are prohibited on trailers.
The number of dipped-beam headlamps shall be two, type approved according to Class C of the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.

The edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be not less than 600 mm apart; this does not apply to M1 and N1 category vehicles.
condition: not applicable to M1 and N1 vehicles

text: For motor vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the dipped-beam headlamps may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: overall width of the vehicle less than 1,300 mm

text: The dipped-beam headlamps shall be at a height of not less than 500 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
For category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height of the dipped-beam headlamps may be increased to 1,500 mm.
condition: off-road (G) vehicles

text: The dipped-beam headlamps shall be at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly, or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the dipped-beam headlamp shall be defined by angles α = 15° upwards and 10° downwards, ß = 45° outwards and 10° inwards.
The presence of partitions or other items of equipment near the dipped-beam headlamp shall not give rise to secondary effects causing discomfort to other road users.
The dipped-beam headlamps shall be oriented towards the front.

The initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the passing-beam shall be set in the unladen vehicle state with one person in the driver's seat, specified within an accuracy of 0.1 per cent by the manufacturer, and within the range defined in paragraph 6.2.6.1.2.

The value of the specified initial downward inclination of the dipped-beam cut-off shall be indicated in a clearly legible and indelible manner on each vehicle close to either headlamp or the manufacturer's plate by the symbol shown in Annex 7.

Different values of the initial downward inclination for different variants/versions of the same vehicle type may be specified within the range of paragraph 6.2.6.1.2., provided that only the pertinent value is indicated on each variant/version.
condition: if different values are specified for variants/versions

text: For a mounting height 0.5 ≤ h ≤ 0.9 m, the vertical inclination of the dipped-beam cut-off shall remain between an upper limit of -0.50 per cent and a lower limit of -(h + 1.2) per cent under all the static loading conditions of Annex 5.

For a mounting height 0.9 < h ≤ 1.2 m, the vertical inclination of the dipped-beam cut-off shall remain between an upper limit of -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) per cent and a lower limit of -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent under all the static loading conditions of Annex 5.
For a mounting height 1.2 < h ≤ 1.5 m, the extension of the aiming diagram for the dipped-beam cut-off inclination limits is only valid for M2G, M3G, N2G, N3G (off-road) vehicles.
condition: 1.2 < h ≤ 1.5 m, off-road (G) vehicles

text: Where a headlamp levelling device is necessary to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 6.2.6.1.1. and 6.2.6.1.2., the device shall be automatic.
condition: if a levelling device is necessary

text: Manually adjusted headlamp levelling devices shall only be permitted for vehicles of categories M2G, M3G, N2G, N3G, provided they have a stop position at which the lamps can be returned to the initial inclination by means of the usual adjusting screws or similar means.
condition: off-road (G) vehicles with manual levelling device

text: Manually adjustable headlamp levelling devices shall be easily visible, reachable and identifiable by the driver in accordance with UN Regulation No. 121.
condition: manual levelling device

text: The number of positions on manual levelling devices shall be such as to ensure compliance with the range of values of paragraph 6.2.6.1.2. in all the loading conditions defined in Annex 5, and the controls shall meet Annex 8.
condition: manual levelling device

text: The different positions to adjust the dipped-beam headlamps shall be explained in the owner's handbook.
condition: manual levelling device

text: In the event of a failure of the headlamp levelling device, the dipped beam shall not assume a position in which the vertical inclination is less downward than it was at the time when the failure occurred.
condition: failure of levelling device

text: After adjustment of the initial downward inclination, the vertical inclination of the dipped beam, expressed in per cent, shall be measured in static conditions under all the loading conditions defined in Annex 5.
The measurement of the variation of dipped-beam downward inclination as a function of load shall be carried out in accordance with the test procedure of Annex 6.

Where the horizontal orientation of the dipped-beam headlamps is varied to produce bend lighting by moving the whole beam or the kink of the elbow of the cut-off, the kink shall not intersect the line of the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle at distances from the front of the vehicle larger than 100 times the mounting height of the respective dipped-beam headlamps.
condition: if horizontal orientation is varied for bend lighting

text: When changing from the main beam to the dipped-beam, all main-beams shall be switched OFF simultaneously.
Gas-discharge light sources of dipped-beam headlamps shall remain switched ON during the main-beam operation.
condition: dipped-beam equipped with gas-discharge light sources

text: One additional light source or one or more LED modules inside the dipped-beam headlamp or in a lamp (except the main-beam headlamp) grouped or reciprocally incorporated with it may be activated to produce bend lighting only when the horizontal radius of curvature of the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle is 500 m or less; this may be demonstrated by calculation or other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.
condition: if additional light source/LED module used for bend lighting

text: The dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched ON and OFF automatically relative to the ambient light conditions according to Annex 13.

Under conditions requiring the dipped-beam headlamps to be ON, they may remain OFF or be switched OFF manually while the automatic transmission control is in the park position, the parking brake is locked, prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the propulsion system, or the front fog lamps are switched ON.
condition: conditions (a), (b), (c) or (e) exist

text: Where manual deactivation of the automatic dipped-beam is provided under condition (d), the control shall be designed so that manual deactivation is not possible with less than two deliberate actions and the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11. shall be switched ON.
condition: condition (d) manual deactivation

text: If the vehicle speed does not exceed 15 km/h, the control shall be designed so that manual deactivation is not possible with less than two deliberate actions, and the lamps of paragraph 5.11. may remain OFF provided that throughout that period it is indicated to the driver with an optical and with an acoustic or haptic warning signal.
condition: vehicle speed not exceeding 15 km/h

text: The automatic operation of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions of paragraph 6.2.7.5.1. no longer exist.
It shall always be possible to switch the dipped-beam headlamps ON manually.
The driver shall at all times be able to engage the automatic operation of the dipped-beam headlamps.
Where the ambient illuminance is 1,000 lx or more, the dipped-beam headlamps may switch ON and OFF automatically relative to other factors such as time or ambient conditions.
condition: ambient illuminance 1,000 lx or more

text: A failure tell-tale for the dipped-beam, flashing or not, is mandatory where the whole beam or the kink of the elbow of the cut-off is moved to produce bend lighting, and shall be activated in the event of a malfunction of the displacement of the kink.
condition: beam or kink moved for bend lighting

text: A failure tell-tale for the dipped-beam is mandatory if one or more light source modules or non-replaceable light sources or more than one UN approved light source produce the principal dipped beam (unless wired so that failure of any one stops all), and shall be activated at the manufacturer's discretion either on failure of any of them or on receipt of a failure signal per paragraph 4.13. of the 01 series of UN Regulation No. 149.
condition: multiple/non-replaceable light sources or modules produce principal dipped beam

text: Once activated, the dipped-beam failure tell-tale shall remain activated while the failure is present; it may be cancelled temporarily but shall be repeated whenever the device which starts and stops the propulsion system is switched ON and OFF.

Dipped-beam headlamps whose light sources/modules producing the principal dipped beam have a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens for at least one headlamp shall only be installed together with headlamp cleaning device(s) according to UN Regulation No. 45.
condition: objective luminous flux exceeds 2,000 lm

text: For filament lamps with more than one test voltage, the objective luminous flux of the principal dipped beam as indicated in the device communication form shall be applied; for approved light sources, the value at the relevant test voltage from the data sheet without tolerances shall be applied.

Bend lighting produced by a horizontal movement of the whole beam or the kink of the elbow of the cut-off shall be switched ON only if the vehicle is in forward motion, except for a right turn in right hand traffic (left turn in left hand traffic).
condition: bend lighting by horizontal beam movement

text: Front fog lamps are optional on motor vehicles and prohibited on trailers.
The number of front fog lamps shall be two, Class F3, type-approved according to the 03 or subsequent series of UN Regulation No. 19 or the 00 or subsequent series of UN Regulation No. 149.
condition: if fitted

text: The point on the apparent surface of the front fog lamp farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The front fog lamps shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles the front fog lamps shall be not more than 800 mm above the ground.
For all other categories except N3G (off-road) vehicles the front fog lamps shall be not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
condition: except N3G

text: For category N3G vehicles the maximum height of the front fog lamps may be increased to 1,500 mm.
condition: N3G off-road vehicles

text: No point on the apparent surface of the front fog lamp shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent surface of the dipped-beam headlamp.

The front fog lamps shall be at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver directly or indirectly through devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces.
The geometric visibility of the front fog lamp shall be defined by α = 5° upwards and downwards, ß = 45° outwards and 10° inwards.
Partitions or other items of equipment near the front fog lamp shall not give rise to secondary effects causing discomfort to other road users.
The front fog lamps shall be oriented toward the front.
The vertical inclination of the front fog lamp cut-off set in the unladen vehicle state with one person in the driver's seat shall be -1.0 per cent or lower.
condition: total objective luminous flux per lamp not exceeding 2,000 lm

text: For h ≤ 0.8 m, the vertical inclination of the front fog lamp cut-off shall automatically remain between -1.0 per cent and -3.0 per cent under all static conditions of Annex 5, with initial aiming between -1.5 per cent and -2.0 per cent.
condition: luminous flux exceeds 2,000 lm, h ≤ 0.8 m

text: For h > 0.8 m, the vertical inclination of the front fog lamp cut-off shall automatically remain between -1.5 per cent and -3.5 per cent under all static conditions of Annex 5, with initial aiming between -2.0 per cent and -2.5 per cent.
condition: luminous flux exceeds 2,000 lm, h > 0.8 m

text: Where a levelling device is fitted for a front fog lamp, the vertical inclination shall remain between the limits of paragraph 6.3.6.1.2.1. under all static loading conditions of Annex 5.
condition: levelling device fitted

text: Where the front fog lamp is part of the dipped-beam headlamp or of an AFS, the requirements of paragraph 6.2.6. shall be applied during use of the front fog beam as part of the dipped beam; these limits may also be applied when the front fog lamp is used as such.
condition: front fog lamp part of dipped beam or AFS

text: The front fog lamp levelling device may automatically adapt the inclination of the front fog beam to prevailing ambient conditions only provided the downward inclination limits of paragraph 6.3.6.1.2.1. are not exceeded.
condition: automatic adaptation used

text: In case of failure of the levelling device, the front fog beam shall not assume a position in which the cut-off is less inclined than at the time of failure.
condition: failure of levelling device

text: It shall be possible to switch the front fog lamps ON and OFF independently of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps or any combination of them, unless they are used as part of another lighting function in an AFS or cannot be simultaneously lit with reciprocally incorporated lamps as indicated by the symbol "/".
Where front fog lamps are used as part of another lighting function in an AFS, switching ON of the front fog lamp function shall have priority over the function of which they are a part.
condition: front fog lamps used in AFS

text: A closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory for the front fog lamps.

The alignment and luminous intensities of the front fog beam may be automatically adapted to prevailing ambient conditions only where the communication form indicates "Luminous intensity is variable", and any variation shall be performed automatically without causing discomfort to the driver or other road users.
condition: positive indication of variable luminous intensity

text: Reversing lamps shall be fitted on motor vehicles.
Reversing lamps shall be fitted on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4.
Reversing lamps are optional on trailers of category O1.
One reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm.
condition: vehicles of category M1 or vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm

text: Two reversing lamp devices are mandatory and two devices are optional on all vehicles with a length exceeding 6,000 mm, except vehicles of category M1.
condition: vehicles with a length exceeding 6,000 mm, except category M1

text: Reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Reversing lamps shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
For category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height of the reversing lamps may be increased to 1,400 mm.
condition: off-road (G) vehicles

text: Reversing lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.

The two optional reversing lamp devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2., if installed, may be fitted on the side of the vehicle only provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. are fulfilled.
condition: optional devices on vehicles exceeding 6,000 mm fitted on the side

text: The geometric visibility of a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angles α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards and β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
condition: only one device installed at the rear

text: The geometric visibility of reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angles α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards and β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
condition: two devices installed at the rear

text: For the two optional reversing lamp devices fitted on the side of the vehicle, the reference axis of the respective device shall be directed outwards with an angle β not exceeding 15° relative to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle; the vertical aim may be directed downwards.
condition: optional devices of paragraph 6.4.2.2. fitted on the side of the vehicle

text: Reversing lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
If the two optional reversing lamp devices are fitted on the side of the vehicle, their orientation shall comply with paragraph 6.4.5.2.
condition: optional devices fitted on the side of the vehicle

text: The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system control device is not in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The electrical connections of the two optional reversing lamp devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. shall be such that they cannot be switched ON unless the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp referred to in paragraph 5.11. are switched ON.
condition: optional devices of paragraph 6.4.2.2.

text: Reversing lamp devices fitted on the side of the vehicle may be switched ON for slow manoeuvres in forward motion up to a maximum speed of 15 km/h only if they are switched ON and OFF manually by a separate control.
condition: side-mounted devices used in forward motion

text: Side-mounted reversing lamp devices switched ON for forward slow manoeuvres shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h, regardless of the position of the separate control, and shall remain switched OFF until deliberately switched ON again.
condition: side-mounted devices used in forward motion

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: Direction-indicator lamps shall be fitted on all vehicles.
Direction-indicator arrangement "A" shall apply to all motor vehicles.
Direction-indicator arrangement "B" shall apply to trailers only.

Direction-indicator lamps shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Arrangement A: two front direction-indicator lamps of category 1, 1a or 1b shall be fitted if the distance between the edge of their apparent surface and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp is at least 40 mm.
condition: distance to dipped-beam headlamp/front fog lamp at least 40 mm

text: Arrangement A: two front direction-indicator lamps of category 1a or 1b shall be fitted if the distance between the edge of their apparent surface and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp is greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm.
condition: distance greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm

text: Arrangement A: two front direction-indicator lamps of category 1b shall be fitted if the distance between the edge of their apparent surface and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp is less than or equal to 20 mm.
condition: distance less than or equal to 20 mm

text: Arrangement A: two rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2a or 2b shall be fitted.
Arrangement A: two optional rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2a or 2b may be fitted on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3.
Arrangement A: two side direction-indicator lamps of at least category 5 shall be fitted on all M1 vehicles and on N1, M2 and M3 vehicles not exceeding 6 metres in length.
condition: M1, or N1/M2/M3 not exceeding 6 m in length

text: Arrangement A: two side direction-indicator lamps of category 6 shall be fitted on all N2 and N3 vehicles and on N1, M2 and M3 vehicles exceeding 6 metres in length.
condition: N2/N3, or N1/M2/M3 exceeding 6 m in length

text: Category 5 side direction-indicator lamps may be replaced by category 6 side direction-indicator lamps in all instances.

Where lamps combining the functions of front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) and side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) are fitted, two additional side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5.
condition: combined front/side direction-indicator lamps fitted

text: Arrangement B: two rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2a or 2b shall be fitted on trailers.
Arrangement B: two optional rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2a or 2b may be fitted on vehicles of categories O2, O3 and O4.
Arrangement B: a maximum of three optional category 5 or one optional category 6 side direction-indicator device per side may be fitted on vehicles of type O2 exceeding 9 m in length.
condition: O2 exceeding 9 m in length

text: Where an AFS is fitted, the distance to be considered for the choice of the front direction-indicator category shall be the distance between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.
condition: AFS fitted

text: On vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3 of above 6 m and up to and including 9 m in length, one additional category 5 side direction-indicator device per side is optional.
condition: length above 6 m up to and including 9 m

text: On vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3 exceeding 9 m in length, three additional category 5 side direction-indicator devices distributed as evenly as practicable along each side are mandatory, unless at least three amber side-marker lamps flash in phase and simultaneously with the direction-indicator lamps on the same side.
condition: length exceeding 9 m and not at least three amber side-marker lamps flashing with the direction indicators

text: On vehicles of categories O3 and O4, three category 5 side direction-indicator devices distributed as evenly as practicable along each side are mandatory, unless at least three amber side-marker lamps flash in phase and simultaneously with the direction-indicator lamps on the same side.
condition: not at least three amber side-marker lamps flashing with the direction indicators

text: The edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the direction-indicator lamp farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this does not apply to the optional rear lamps.
condition: except optional rear lamps

text: The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the direction-indicator lamps shall not be less than 600 mm; this may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The height of the light-emitting surface of side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6, measured from the lowest point, shall not be less than 350 mm for M1 and N1 vehicles.
condition: side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6

text: The height of the light-emitting surface of side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6, measured from the lowest point, shall not be less than 500 mm for all vehicle categories other than M1 and N1.
condition: side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 on vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: The height of the light-emitting surface of side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6, measured from the highest point, shall not be more than 1,500 mm.
condition: side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6

text: The height of direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, measured in accordance with paragraph 5.8., shall not be less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.

If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limits to be respected and the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper limit may be increased to 2,300 mm for side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 and 6.
condition: vehicle structure does not permit 1,500 mm and optional rear lamps not installed

text: If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limits to be respected and the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper limit may be increased to 2,100 mm for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.
