condition: vehicle structure does not permit 1,500 mm and optional rear lamps not installed

text: If optional rear direction-indicator lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the requirements of paragraph 6.5.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
condition: optional rear lamps installed

text: The distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane marking the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 1,800 mm.
For M1 and N1 vehicles, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the forward boundary of the vehicle shall not exceed 2,500 mm.

For vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp and the forward boundary of the vehicle shall not exceed 2,500 mm if the structure of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with the minimum angles of visibility.
condition: structure makes it impossible to comply with minimum visibility angles

text: Optional category 5 side direction-indicator lamps shall be fitted, spaced evenly, along the length of the vehicle.
condition: optional category 5 lamps fitted

text: An optional category 6 side direction-indicator lamp shall be fitted in the area between the first and last quartiles of the length of a trailer.
condition: optional category 6 lamp fitted

text: The geometric visibility of direction-indicator lamps shall meet the horizontal angles shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.1, with the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator not exceeding 5° (d ≤ 1.80 m; for M1 and N1 vehicles d ≤ 2.50 m).
The vertical angles of geometric visibility of direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b and 5 shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where a direction-indicator lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
condition: lamp mounted below 750 mm

text: Where an optional rear direction-indicator lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
condition: optional rear lamp mounted above 2,100 mm

text: The vertical angles of geometric visibility of direction-indicator lamps of category 6 shall be 30° above and 5° below the horizontal.
For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
condition: lamp mounted below 750 mm

text: At the discretion of the manufacturer, for M1 and N1 vehicles, front and rear direction-indicator lamps as well as side-marker lamps may meet the alternative horizontal angles shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.2, with the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator not exceeding 5° (d ≤ 2.50 m).
condition: manufacturer opts for the alternative arrangement

text: Under the alternative arrangement for M1 and N1 vehicles, for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm, the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
condition: alternative arrangement; lamp mounted below 750 mm

text: Under the alternative arrangement for M1 and N1 vehicles, the vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
condition: alternative arrangement

text: Under the alternative arrangement, to be considered visible the direction-indicator lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, except for side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6; the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
condition: alternative arrangement

text: Direction-indicator lamps shall be oriented according to the specifications for installation by the manufacturer, if any.
condition: if manufacturer installation specifications exist

text: Direction-indicator lamps shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control and shall flash in phase.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps.
condition: vehicle less than 6 m in length with arrangement per 6.5.5.2. and amber side-marker lamps mounted

text: A direction indicator capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential) shall not switch between both modes once activated.
condition: direction indicator capable of static and sequential modes

text: If two optional rear direction-indicator lamps (category 2a or 2b) are installed on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, they shall be operated in the same mode (static or sequential) as the mandatory rear direction-indicator lamps.
condition: optional rear lamps installed

text: An operating tell-tale is mandatory for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b; it may be visual or auditory or both.
condition: mandatory direction-indicator lamps

text: If the direction-indicator tell-tale is visual, it shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, is either extinguished, or remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency.
condition: visual tell-tale

text: If the direction-indicator tell-tale is entirely auditory, it shall be clearly audible and shall show a marked change of frequency, at least in the event of malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.
condition: entirely auditory tell-tale

text: The direction-indicator operating tell-tale shall be activated by the signal produced according to paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 6, paragraph 5.6.3. of the 00 series of UN Regulation No. 148, paragraph 4.6.1.4. of the 01 series of UN Regulation No. 148, or another suitable way.

A motor vehicle equipped to draw a trailer shall be fitted with a special visual operational tell-tale for the direction-indicator lamps on the trailer, unless the tell-tale of the drawing vehicle allows the failure of any one of the direction-indicator lamps on the vehicle combination to be detected.
condition: motor vehicle equipped to draw a trailer

text: The direction-indicator light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.
Operation of the direction-indicator light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light.
Operation of the direction-indicator light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one and one-half seconds by the first extinction of the light.
If a motor vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the control of the direction-indicator lamps on the drawing vehicle shall also operate the indicator lamps of the trailer.
condition: motor vehicle equipped to draw a trailer

text: In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the others shall continue to flash; the frequency in this condition may differ from that prescribed.
condition: failure (other than short-circuit) of one direction-indicator lamp

text: A hazard warning signal shall be fitted on all vehicles.
The hazard warning signal shall be given by simultaneous operation of the direction-indicator lamps in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 6.5.
All direction indicators of category 1 (1, 1a, 1b) activated simultaneously as hazard warning signal shall operate in the same mode, i.e. static or sequential.
All direction indicators of category 2 (2a, 2b) activated simultaneously as hazard warning signal shall operate in the same mode, i.e. static or sequential.
The number of lamps of the hazard warning signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.2.
The arrangement of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.3.
The position in width of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.1.
The position in height of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.2.
The position in length of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.3.
The geometric visibility of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.5.
The orientation of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.6.
The hazard warning signal shall be operated by means of a separate manual control enabling all the direction-indicator lamps to flash in phase.

The hazard warning signal may be switched ON automatically only in the event of a vehicle being involved in a collision, after the emergency stop signal has been switched OFF as specified in paragraph 6.23., or to indicate the risk of imminent danger as defined by Regulations; when switched ON automatically after a collision or emergency stop signal, it may be switched OFF manually.
condition: automatic switching ON

text: When the hazard warning signal is switched ON automatically to indicate to other road users the risk of imminent danger, it shall remain switched ON until it is manually or automatically switched OFF.
condition: automatically switched ON for imminent danger

text: On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps when the hazard warning signal operates.
condition: vehicle less than 6 m in length with arrangement per 6.5.5.2. and amber side-marker lamps mounted

text: A flashing closed-circuit tell-tale for the hazard warning signal is mandatory.
The hazard warning signal shall flash 90 ± 30 times per minute and meet the switching timing, trailer and failure requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.9.
If a power-driven vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the hazard warning signal control shall also be capable of bringing the direction-indicator lamps on the trailer into action.
condition: vehicle equipped to draw a trailer

text: The hazard warning signal shall be able to function even if the device which starts or stops the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible to start the propulsion system.
Stop lamps of category S1 or S2 shall be fitted on all categories of vehicles.

A stop lamp of category S3 or S4 shall be fitted on vehicles of categories M1 and N1, except for chassis-cabs and N1 category vehicles with open cargo space; it is optional on other categories of vehicles.
condition: except chassis-cabs and N1 vehicles with open cargo space

text: The number of stop lamps shall be two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device on all categories of vehicles.
The stop lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Two optional category S1 or S2 stop lamps may be installed on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O2, O3 and O4 only where no category S3 or S4 device is installed.
condition: if no category S3 or S4 device is installed

text: Only when the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle is not located on a fixed body panel but separates one or two movable parts of the vehicle (e.g. doors) and lacks sufficient space to install a single S3 or S4 device on the median longitudinal plane above such movable parts, either two S3 or S4 category devices of type "D" may be installed, or one S3 or S4 device may be installed offset to the left or right of the median longitudinal plane, or an interdependent lamp system of category S3 or S4 may be installed.
condition: median longitudinal plane separates movable parts and lacks space for a single S3/S4 device

text: For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of S1 or S2 stop lamps which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: S1 or S2 category devices

text: For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of S1 or S2 stop lamps shall be not less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: S1 or S2 category devices on vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: For S3 or S4 category stop lamps, the centre of reference shall be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
condition: S3 or S4 category device

text: Where two S3 or S4 category stop lamps are installed according to paragraph 6.7.2., they shall be positioned as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane, one on each side of this plane.
condition: two S3 or S4 devices installed per paragraph 6.7.2.2

text: Where one S3 or S4 category stop lamp offset from the median longitudinal plane is permitted according to paragraph 6.7.2., the offset shall not exceed 150 mm from the median longitudinal plane to the centre of reference of the lamp.
condition: one offset S3 or S4 device permitted per paragraph 6.7.2.2

text: S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
condition: S1 or S2 category devices

text: If optional S1 or S2 stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
condition: if optional S1 or S2 lamps are installed

text: For S3 or S4 category stop lamps, the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall either not be more than 150 mm below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the exposed surface of the glass or glazing of the rear window, or not be less than 850 mm above the ground.
condition: S3 or S4 category device

text: The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of an S3 or S4 category stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamps.
condition: S3 or S4 category device

text: S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
condition: S1 or S2 category devices

text: The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; for S1 and S2 lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
condition: S1 or S2 category devices

text: The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of S3 or S4 category stop lamps shall be 10° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
condition: S3 or S4 category device

text: The vertical angle of geometric visibility of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.
condition: S1 or S2 category devices

text: The vertical angle of geometric visibility of S3 or S4 category stop lamps shall be 10° above and 5° below the horizontal.
condition: S3 or S4 category device

text: Stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
condition: propulsion system cannot operate

text: A tell-tale for the stop lamps is optional; however a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: The S3 or S4 category stop lamp shall not be reciprocally incorporated with any other lamp.
condition: S3 or S4 category device
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Where the S3 or S4 category stop lamp is installed inside the vehicle, the light emitted shall not cause discomfort to the driver through the devices for indirect vision and/or other surfaces of the vehicle (i.e. rear window).
condition: S3 or S4 device installed inside the vehicle

text: The rear registration plate lamp shall be fitted (mandatory).
The number of rear registration plate lamps shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.

Rear registration plate lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 4, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The arrangement of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The position in width of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The position in height of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The position in length of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The geometric visibility of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The orientation of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The electrical connections of the rear registration plate lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
If a tell-tale for the rear registration plate lamp exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
condition: if a tell-tale exists

text: When the rear registration plate lamp is combined with the rear position lamp, reciprocally incorporated in the stop lamp or in the rear fog lamp, its photometric characteristics may be modified only during the entire time the stop lamp or the rear fog lamp is switched ON.
condition: combined with rear position lamp, reciprocally incorporated in stop lamp or rear fog lamp
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Front position lamps shall be fitted on all motor vehicles and on trailers over 1,600 mm wide; they are optional on trailers not more than 1,600 mm wide.
condition: trailers only if over 1,600 mm wide

text: The number of front position lamps shall be two.
Front position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the front position lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

In the case of a trailer, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the front position lamp which is farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 150 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the front position lamps shall be not less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: Front position lamps shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm for O1 and O2 categories of vehicles, or for any other categories if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Where the front position lamp and another lamp are reciprocally incorporated, the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the other lamp shall be used to verify compliance with the positioning requirements of paragraphs 6.9.4.1. to 6.9.4.3.
condition: front position lamp reciprocally incorporated with another lamp
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of front position lamps shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane, and in the case of trailers the inward angle may be reduced to 5°.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility of front position lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed, the geometric visibility of front position lamps shall be horizontal 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane for lamps mounted below 750 mm) and vertical 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle may be reduced to 5° for lamps mounted below 750 mm).
condition: alternative chosen by manufacturer and a front side-marker lamp is installed

text: When the alternative geometric visibility is used, to be considered visible the front position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
condition: alternative geometric visibility of paragraph 6.9.5.2 used

text: Front position lamps shall be oriented forwards.

The electrical connections of front position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.; if a front position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the front position lamp on the relevant side (or the reciprocally incorporated part) may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.

A closed-circuit tell-tale for the front position lamps is mandatory and shall be non-flashing; it is not required if the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps. This requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
condition: not while daytime running lamps are switched ON

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the front position lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: Infrared radiation generator(s) installed inside the front position lamp shall be allowed to be switched ON only when the headlamp on the same side of the vehicle is switched ON and the vehicle is in forward motion.
condition: if infrared radiation generator(s) installed inside the front position lamp

text: In the event that the front position lamp or the headlamp on the same side fails, the infrared radiation generator(s) inside the front position lamp shall be automatically switched OFF.
condition: if infrared radiation generator(s) installed inside the front position lamp

text: The front position lamp may be swivelled only together with a lighting unit to which it is reciprocally incorporated, in case an AFS providing a bending mode is installed.
condition: AFS providing a bending mode installed

text: Rear position lamps of categories R, R1 or R2 shall be fitted (mandatory).
The number of rear position lamps shall be two.
Rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Two optional rear position lamps may be installed on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O2, O3 and O4 only where end-outline marker lamps are not installed.
condition: end-outline marker lamps not installed

text: The point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this does not apply to the optional rear lamps.
condition: mandatory rear position lamps

text: For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the rear position lamps shall be not less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: Rear position lamps shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

If optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
condition: if optional rear position lamps are installed

text: Rear position lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.

The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of rear position lamps shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility of rear position lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm the downward angle may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed, the geometric visibility of rear position lamps shall be horizontal 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane for lamps mounted below 750 mm) and vertical 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle may be reduced to 5° for lamps mounted below 750 mm).
condition: alternative chosen by manufacturer and a rear side-marker lamp is installed

text: When the alternative geometric visibility is used, to be considered visible the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
condition: alternative geometric visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2 used

text: Rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.; if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the rear position lamp on the relevant side (or the reciprocally incorporated part) may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.

A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps is mandatory and shall be combined with that of the front position lamps. This requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
condition: not when daytime running lamps are switched ON

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: Rear fog lamps of categories F, F1 or F2 shall be fitted (mandatory).
The number of rear fog lamps shall be one or two.
Rear fog lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 38, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

If there is only one rear fog lamp, it shall be on the opposite side of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle to the direction of traffic prescribed in the country of registration; the centre of reference may also be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
condition: if only one rear fog lamp is fitted

text: Rear fog lamps shall be not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,000 mm above the ground; for rear fog lamps grouped with any rear lamp the maximum height may be increased to 1,200 mm, and for N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles to 1,400 mm.
Rear fog lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of rear fog lamps shall be defined by angles α = 5° upwards and 5° downwards and ß = 25° to right and to left.
Rear fog lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
The electrical connections shall be such that the rear fog lamp(s) cannot be switched ON unless the main beams, dipped-beams or front fog lamps are switched ON.
The electrical connections shall be such that the rear fog lamp(s) can be switched OFF independently of any other lamp.
The electrical connections of the rear fog lamp(s) shall satisfy either paragraph 6.11.7.3.1. or paragraph 6.11.7.3.2.
The rear fog lamp(s) may continue to operate until the position lamps are switched OFF, and shall then remain OFF until deliberately switched ON again.
condition: if option 6.11.7.3.1 is chosen

text: A warning, at least audible, additional to the mandatory tell-tale shall be given if the ignition is switched OFF or the ignition key is withdrawn and the driver's door is opened, whether the lamps in paragraph 6.11.7.1. are ON or OFF, whilst the rear fog lamp control is in the ON position.
condition: if option 6.11.7.3.2 is chosen

text: Except as provided in paragraphs 6.11.7.1., 6.11.7.3. and 6.11.7.5., the operation of the rear fog lamp(s) shall not be affected by switching ON or OFF any other lamps.
The rear fog lamp(s) of a drawing motor vehicle may be automatically switched OFF only while a trailer is connected and the rear fog lamp(s) of the trailer is (are) switched ON.
condition: trailer connected with its rear fog lamp(s) switched ON

text: A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear fog lamp(s) is mandatory.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear fog lamp(s) is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: In all cases, the distance between the rear fog lamp and each stop lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.
Parking lamps are optional on motor vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length.
condition: motor vehicle length not exceeding 6 m

text: Parking lamps are prohibited on all vehicles other than motor vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length.
condition: motor vehicles exceeding 6 m in length and all trailers

text: The number of parking lamps shall be according to the arrangement.
condition: if parking lamps are fitted

text: Parking lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 77, or to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
condition: if parking lamps are fitted

text: Parking lamps shall be arranged either as two lamps at the front and two lamps at the rear, or one lamp on each side.
condition: if parking lamps are fitted

text: In width, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the parking lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: if parking lamps are fitted

text: If there are two parking lamps, they shall be on the sides of the vehicle.
condition: if there are two parking lamps

text: For vehicles other than M1 and N1, parking lamps shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
condition: vehicles of categories other than M1 and N1

text: The geometric visibility of parking lamps shall be, horizontally, 45° outwards, forwards and rearwards; where a front or rear parking lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility of parking lamps shall be, vertically, 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Parking lamps shall be oriented such that the lamps meet the requirements for visibility forwards and rearwards.
The electrical connection shall allow the parking lamp(s) on the same side of the vehicle to be switched ON independently of any other lamps.

The parking lamp(s) and, if applicable, the front and rear position lamps used according to paragraph 6.12.9., shall be able to operate even if the device which starts the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A device which automatically switches OFF the parking lamps (or the position lamps used as parking lamps) as a function of time is prohibited.
If a closed-circuit tell-tale for the parking lamps is fitted (optional), it shall not be possible to confuse it with the tell-tale for the front and rear position lamps.
condition: if a parking lamp tell-tale is fitted

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the parking lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: The parking lamp function may be performed by simultaneously switching ON the front and rear position lamps on the same side of the vehicle; in this case lamps meeting the requirements of front or rear position lamps are deemed to meet the requirements of parking lamps.
condition: if parking function is performed by position lamps

text: End-outline marker lamps of categories A or AM (visible from the front) and R, R1, R2, RM1 or RM2 (visible from the rear) are mandatory on vehicles exceeding 2.10 m in width.
condition: vehicle width exceeding 2.10 m

text: End-outline marker lamps are optional on vehicles between 1.80 and 2.10 m in width; on chassis-cabs the rear end-outline marker lamps are optional.
condition: vehicle width between 1.80 and 2.10 m, or chassis-cabs for rear lamps

text: End-outline marker lamps shall number two visible from the front and two visible from the rear; additional lamps may be fitted as two visible from the front and two visible from the rear.

End-outline marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

In width, front and rear end-outline marker lamps shall be as close as possible to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this is deemed met when the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the median longitudinal plane is not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

On motor vehicles, the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the front end-outline marker lamp shall not be lower than the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the transparent zone of the wind-screen.
condition: front lamps on motor vehicles

text: On trailers and semi-trailers, front end-outline marker lamps shall be at the maximum height compatible with the requirements relating to the width, design and operational requirements of the vehicle and to the symmetry of the lamps.
condition: front lamps on trailers and semi-trailers

text: Rear end-outline marker lamps shall be at the maximum height compatible with the requirements relating to the width, design and operational requirements of the vehicle and to the symmetry of the lamps.
condition: rear lamps

text: The additional rear end-outline marker lamps (paragraph 6.13.2.(b)) shall be fitted as far separated in height as practicable in respect to the mandatory ones, provided that their position is compatible with design/operational requirements of the vehicle and symmetry of the lamps.
condition: if additional lamps visible from the rear are fitted

text: The additional front-visible end-outline marker lamps (paragraph 6.13.2.(a)) shall be fitted as close as practicable to the rear; this is deemed satisfied if the distance between the additional lamps and the rear of the vehicle does not exceed 400 mm.
condition: if additional lamps visible from the front are fitted

text: The geometric visibility of end-outline marker lamps shall be: horizontal angle 80° outwards; vertical angle 5° above and 20° below the horizontal.
End-outline marker lamps shall be oriented such that the lamps meet the requirements for visibility forwards and rearwards.
The electrical connections of end-outline marker lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
If an end-outline marker lamp tell-tale exists (optional), its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
condition: if a tell-tale exists

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the end-outline marker lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: Provided that all other requirements are met, the mandatory or optional end-outline marker lamps visible from the front and those visible from the rear on the same side of the vehicle may be combined into one device.
condition: provided all other requirements are met
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Two of the end-outline marker lamps visible from the rear may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated only in accordance with paragraph 5.7.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: The distance between the projections on a transverse vertical plane of the points nearest to one another on the apparent surfaces in the direction of the respective reference axes of an end-outline marker lamp and the corresponding position lamp shall be not less than 200 mm.

The additional end-outline marker lamps (paragraph 6.13.2.(a)) used to mark the rear end outline of the vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer shall be fitted so as to be visible within the fields of vision of the approved main rear-view devices for indirect vision.
condition: if additional lamps visible from the front are fitted

text: Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, are mandatory on motor vehicles.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, are optional on trailers only provided that they are grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.
condition: trailers

text: Two rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be fitted, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional rear retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
condition: if additional retro-reflecting devices are fitted

text: In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the rear non-triangular retro-reflector farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear non-triangular retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm; this may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: Rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
Rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be horizontally 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be vertically 10° above and below horizontal; where mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the rear non-triangular retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Rear triangular retro-reflectors are mandatory on trailers.
Rear triangular retro-reflectors are prohibited on motor vehicles.

Two rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be fitted, type-approved as Class IIIA or Class IIIB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional rear retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.15.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
condition: if additional retro-reflecting devices are fitted

text: The apex of the triangle of the rear triangular retro-reflector shall be directed upwards.

In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the rear triangular retro-reflector farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The inner edges of the rear triangular retro-reflectors shall not be less than 600 mm apart; this may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

Rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
Rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be horizontally 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be vertically 15° above and below the horizontal; where mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the rear triangular retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Front non-triangular retro-reflectors are mandatory on trailers.
Front non-triangular retro-reflectors are mandatory on motor vehicles having all forward facing lamps with reflectors concealable, and optional on other motor vehicles.
condition: mandatory if all forward facing lamps with reflectors are concealable

text: Two front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be fitted, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional front retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.16.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
condition: if additional retro-reflecting devices are fitted

text: In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the front non-triangular retro-reflector farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

In the case of a trailer, the point of the illuminating surface of the front non-triangular retro-reflector farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be farther than 150 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: trailers

text: For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the front non-triangular retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm; this may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
condition: vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: Front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm).
Front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be in length at the front of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be horizontally 30° inwards and outwards; in the case of trailers the angle inwards may be reduced to 10°.

If because of the construction of a trailer the horizontal visibility angle cannot be met by the mandatory front retro-reflectors, additional (supplementary) retro-reflectors shall be fitted, without the width limitation of paragraph 6.16.4.1., which, in conjunction with the mandatory retro-reflectors, give the necessary visibility angle.
condition: if the trailer construction prevents the mandatory retro-reflectors meeting the angle

text: The geometric visibility of front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be vertically 10° above and below the horizontal; where mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Front non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be oriented towards the front.
The illuminating surface of the front non-triangular retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the front.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Side non-triangular retro-reflectors are mandatory on all motor vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m and on all trailers.
condition: motor vehicles exceeding 6 m in length and all trailers

text: Side non-triangular retro-reflectors are optional on motor vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m.
condition: motor vehicle length not exceeding 6 m

text: The number of side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be such that the requirements for longitudinal positioning are complied with.

Side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional side retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.17.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
condition: if additional retro-reflecting devices are fitted

text: Side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively or if the presence of the device is not mandatory according to paragraph 6.17.1.).
At least one side retro-reflector shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle, the foremost side retro-reflector being not further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front.
condition: vehicles exceeding 6 m in length (motor vehicles) and trailers, unless alternative provisions apply

text: The distance between two adjacent side retro-reflectors shall not exceed 3 m (except M1 and N1 vehicles); if the structure, design or operational use of the vehicle makes compliance impossible, this distance may be increased to 4 m.
condition: vehicles other than M1 and N1

text: The distance between the rearmost side retro-reflector and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.
condition: vehicles exceeding 6 m in length (motor vehicles) and trailers

text: For motor vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m, it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector fitted within the first third and/or one within the last third of the vehicle length.
condition: motor vehicle length not exceeding 6 m

text: For M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m, it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.
condition: vehicle length exceeding 6 m but not exceeding 7 m

text: The geometric visibility of side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be horizontally 45° to the front and to the rear.

The geometric visibility of side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be vertically 10° above and below the horizontal; where mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Side non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be oriented towards the side.
The illuminating surface of the side retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other side lamp.
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Side-marker lamps shall be mandatory on all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.
condition: vehicle length exceeds 6 m and vehicle is not a chassis-cab

text: The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles where side-marker lamps are mandatory; however the SM2 type of side-marker lamps may be used on the M1 category of vehicles.
condition: side-marker lamps mandatory

text: On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
condition: vehicle length less than 6 m and position lamps use reduced geometric visibility of 6.9.5.2./6.10.5.2.

text: Side-marker lamps are optional on all other vehicles; the SM1 or SM2 types of side-marker lamps may be used.
condition: side-marker lamps optional

text: The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
Side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Side-marker lamps shall be at a height above the ground of not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
At least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle, the foremost side-marker lamp being not further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front.

The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m; if the structure, design or the operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with such a requirement, this distance may be increased to 4 m.
The distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.

For vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m and for chassis-cabs it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length.
condition: vehicle length not exceeding 6 m or chassis-cab

text: For M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.
condition: vehicle length exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m

text: The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of side-marker lamps shall be 45° to the front and to the rear; for vehicles on which the installation of the side-marker lamps is optional this value can be reduced to 30°.

If the vehicle is equipped with side-marker lamps used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the horizontal angles of the side-marker lamps shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.
condition: side-marker lamps supplement reduced geometric visibility of direction indicators or position lamps

text: The vertical angle of geometric visibility of side-marker lamps shall be 10° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Side-marker lamps shall be oriented towards the side.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length amber side-marker lamps may be wired to flash, provided that this flashing is in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.
condition: vehicle length less than 6 m and amber side-marker lamps wired to flash

text: On M2, M3, N2, N3, O3 and O4 vehicles mandatory amber side-marker lamps may flash simultaneously with the direction-indicator lamps on the same side of the vehicle.
condition: mandatory amber side-marker lamps

text: Where there are direction indicator lamps of category 5 installed according to paragraph 6.5.3.1. on the side of the vehicle, the amber side-marker lamps shall not flash.
condition: category 5 direction indicator lamps installed on the side according to 6.5.3.1.

text: A tell-tale for side-marker lamps is optional; if it exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
condition: if a tell-tale exists

text: A tell-tale indicating failure of side-marker lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: When the rearmost side-marker lamp is combined with the rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with the rear fog lamp or stop lamp, the photometric characteristics of the side-marker lamp may be modified during the entire time the rear fog lamp or stop lamp is switched ON.
condition: rearmost side-marker lamp combined with rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with rear fog lamp or stop lamp
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Rear side-marker lamps shall be amber if they flash with the rear direction-indicator lamp.
condition: rear side-marker lamps flash with rear direction-indicator lamp

text: When an optional side-marker lamp is grouped or combined with a position lamp that is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the direction indicator, the electrical connection of the side-marker lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the direction indicator lamp.
condition: optional side-marker lamp grouped or combined with position lamp reciprocally incorporated or grouped with direction indicator
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: Daytime running lamps shall be mandatory on motor vehicles and prohibited on trailers.

Two daytime running lamps shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 87, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the daytime running lamps shall not be less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
Daytime running lamps shall be at a height above the ground of not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm.

Daytime running lamps shall be at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of daytime running lamps shall be horizontal: outwards 20° and inwards 20°; vertical: upwards 10° and downwards 10°.
Daytime running lamps shall be oriented towards the front.

The daytime running lamps shall be switched ON automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it possible for the propulsion system to operate and neither of the following exist: (a) the front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

Under conditions requiring the daytime running lamps to be switched ON, the daytime running lamps may remain OFF or, once automatically switched ON, may be switched OFF manually and remain OFF only while at least one of the following exists: (a) automatic transmission control in park position; (b) parking brake in locked position; (c) prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system; (d) vehicle speed does not exceed 15 km/h.
condition: at least one of the listed conditions exists

text: The automatic operation of the daytime running lamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions described in paragraph 6.19.7.2. no longer exist.

The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.

The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when either of the following exists: (a) the front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.
When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON; any other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may also be switched ON.
condition: daytime running lamps switched ON

text: The rear position lamps and the other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain switched OFF only as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to Annex 13).
condition: ambient light above 7,000 lux

text: If a front direction-indicator lamp is not reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp and the distance between the edges of their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis is equal to or less than 40 mm, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the daytime running lamp on the relevant side is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp; or (b) its luminous intensity is reduced during the entire period of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp to not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility.
condition: front direction-indicator not reciprocally incorporated with DRL and distance between apparent surfaces ≤ 40 mm

text: The conformity of the reduced daytime running lamp intensity (not more than 140 cd) shall be verified at the time of the daytime running lamp type approval and indicated in the related communication form.
condition: option (b) of 6.19.7.6 used

text: If the luminous intensity of the front direction-indicator lamp in HV is at least 50% higher than that of the daytime running lamp in HV, the daytime running lamp need not be switched OFF nor dimmed; in this case the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority.
condition: front direction-indicator HV intensity at least 50% higher than DRL HV intensity

text: If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with totally common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections shall be such that the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp.
condition: front direction-indicator reciprocally incorporated with DRL with totally common apparent surfaces
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with partially common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the whole daytime running lamp function on the relevant side is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the front direction-indicator lamp; or (b) for category 1a or 1b front direction-indicator lamps, the daytime running lamp function is switched OFF for the part of the apparent surface in common and the luminous intensity of the part not in common is reduced during the entire period of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp to not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility.
condition: front direction-indicator reciprocally incorporated with DRL with partially common apparent surfaces
applies_to: grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp

text: The conformity of the reduced intensity of the non-common part of the daytime running lamp (not more than 140 cd) shall be verified at the time of the daytime running lamp type approval and indicated in the related communication form.
condition: option (b) of 6.19.7.7.2 used

text: A closed-circuit tell-tale for daytime running lamps is optional; a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: failure tell-tale if required by the component regulation

text: Cornering lamps are optional on motor vehicles.

Two cornering lamps shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 119, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
condition: if cornering lamps are fitted

text: One cornering lamp shall be located on each side of the vehicle's median longitudinal plane.
Cornering lamps shall be positioned in length not further than 1,000 mm from the front.
Cornering lamps shall be at a height not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm above the ground.

No point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the cornering lamp shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp.
The geometric visibility of cornering lamps shall be defined by angles α = 10° upwards and downwards and β = 30° to 60° outwards.
Cornering lamps shall be oriented such that the lamps meet the requirements for geometric visibility.
The cornering lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be switched ON unless the main-beam headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps are switched ON at the same time.

The cornering lamp on one side of the vehicle may only be switched ON automatically when the direction-indicators on the same side are switched ON and/or when the steering angle is changed from the straight-ahead position towards the same side.
The cornering lamp shall be switched OFF automatically when the direction-indicator is switched OFF and/or the steering angle has returned to the straight-ahead position.

When the reversing lamp is switched ON, both cornering lamps may be switched ON simultaneously, independently from the steering wheel position or direction-indicator operation; if so switched ON, both cornering lamps shall be switched OFF either (a) when the reversing lamp is switched OFF; or (b) when the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h.
condition: cornering lamps switched ON with reversing lamp

text: No tell-tale is required for cornering lamps; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
condition: if required by the component regulation

text: The cornering lamps shall not be switched ON at vehicle speeds above 40 km/h.
Conspicuity markings are prohibited on vehicles of categories M1 and O1.

Full contour marking to the rear is mandatory on vehicles exceeding 2,100 mm in width of category N2 with a maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes and N3 (with the exception of chassis-cabs, incomplete vehicles and tractors for semi-trailers).
condition: vehicle width exceeding 2,100 mm; N2 with maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes; not chassis-cab, incomplete vehicle or tractor for semi-trailer

text: Full contour marking to the rear is mandatory on vehicles exceeding 2,100 mm in width of categories O3 and O4 (with the exception of incomplete vehicles).
condition: vehicle width exceeding 2,100 mm; not an incomplete vehicle

text: Partial contour marking to the side is mandatory on vehicles exceeding 6,000 mm in length of category N2 with a maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes and N3 (with the exception of chassis-cabs, incomplete vehicles and tractors for semi-trailers).
condition: vehicle length exceeding 6,000 mm; N2 with maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes; not chassis-cab, incomplete vehicle or tractor for semi-trailer

text: Partial contour marking to the side is mandatory on vehicles of categories O3 and O4 exceeding 6,000 mm in length (including the drawbar) (with the exception of incomplete vehicles).
condition: vehicle length including drawbar exceeding 6,000 mm; not an incomplete vehicle

text: A line marking may be installed instead of the mandatory contour marking only if the shape, structure, design or operational requirements of the vehicle make it impossible to install the mandatory contour marking.
condition: if impossible to install the mandatory contour marking

text: If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are partially constituted of flexible material, the line marking shall be installed on rigid part(s) of the vehicle; the remaining portion of conspicuity markings may be fitted on the flexible material.
condition: if bodywork exterior surfaces are partially of flexible material

text: If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are constituted fully of flexible material, the line marking may be fitted on the flexible material.
condition: if bodywork exterior surfaces are fully of flexible material

text: Partial fulfilment of the conspicuity marking requirements of paragraphs 6.21.2. to 6.21.7.5. is acceptable only where the manufacturer, after verification by the Technical Service, proves to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that compliance is impossible due to operational requirements requiring special shape, structure or design, and conditional upon a portion of the requirements being met where possible and the application of conspicuity markings that partially meet requirements being maximised on the vehicle structure.
condition: where full compliance is proven impossible due to operational requirements

text: Additional brackets or plates fitted for partial fulfilment shall contain material type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 104 or to UN Regulation No. 150, where structure is available to ensure clear and uniform signalling compatible with the objective of conspicuity.
condition: where partial fulfilment is deemed acceptable and additional brackets or plates are fitted

text: Where partial fulfilment is deemed acceptable, retro-reflective devices of Class IVA type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3 or the 00 or subsequent series to UN Regulation No. 150, or brackets containing retro-reflecting material type-approved to Class C photometric requirements of UN Regulation No. 104 or No. 150, may substitute part of the required conspicuity markings, in which case at least one of these retro-reflective devices shall be installed per 1,500 mm.
condition: where partial fulfilment is deemed acceptable and retro-reflective devices substitute part of the markings

text: Where partial fulfilment of the conspicuity marking requirements is accepted, the necessary information shall be indicated in the communication form.
condition: where partial fulfilment is deemed acceptable

text: Conspicuity markings to the rear and to the side are optional on all other categories of vehicles not otherwise specified in paragraphs 6.21.1.1. and 6.21.1.2., including the cab of tractor units for semi-trailers and the cab of chassis-cabs.
condition: vehicles not covered by 6.21.1.1 or 6.21.1.2

text: Partial or full contour marking may be applied instead of mandatory line markings, and full contour marking may be applied instead of mandatory partial contour marking.
Line marking to the front is optional on vehicles of categories O2, O3 and O4.
Partial or full contour marking shall not be applied to the front of the vehicle.
The number of conspicuity markings shall be according to the presence requirements.

The conspicuity markings shall be as close as practicable to horizontal and vertical, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operational requirements of the vehicle; if this is not possible, the full or partial contour markings, when fitted, shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
The conspicuity markings shall be spaced as evenly as possible over the horizontal dimensions of the vehicle such that the total length and/or width of the vehicle can be identified.
The conspicuity marking shall be as close as practicable to the edge of the vehicle.

The cumulative horizontal length of the conspicuity marking elements, as mounted on the vehicle, shall equate to at least 70 per cent of the overall width of the vehicle, excluding any horizontal overlap of individual elements.
The side conspicuity marking shall be as close as practicable to the ends of the vehicle and reach to within 600 mm of each end of the vehicle.
For motor vehicles, the conspicuity marking shall reach to within 600 mm of each end of the vehicle, or in the case of tractors for semi-trailers each end of the cab.
condition: motor vehicles

text: An alternative marking mode within 2,400 mm from the front end of the motor vehicle is allowed where a series of retro-reflectors of Class IVA (UN Regulation No. 3, 02 or subsequent series, or UN Regulation No. 150) or Class C (UN Regulation No. 104 or No. 150) is mounted followed by the required conspicuity marking, with a retro-reflector size of minimum 25 cm2.
condition: if the alternative marking mode is used

text: In the alternative marking mode, one retro-reflector shall be mounted not more than 600 mm from the front end of the vehicle.
condition: if the alternative marking mode is used

text: In the alternative marking mode, additional retro-reflectors shall be spaced not more than 600 mm apart.
condition: if the alternative marking mode is used

text: In the alternative marking mode, the distance between the last retro-reflector and the start of the conspicuity marking shall not exceed 600 mm.
condition: if the alternative marking mode is used

text: For trailers, the conspicuity marking shall reach to within 600 mm of each end of the vehicle (excluding the drawbar).
condition: trailers

text: For motor vehicles, the cumulative horizontal length of the side conspicuity marking elements, excluding any horizontal overlap, shall equate to at least 70 per cent of the length of the vehicle, or in the case of tractors for semi-trailers, if fitted, the length of the cab; when using the alternative marking mode, of the distance beginning within 2,400 mm from the front end of the vehicle to its rear end.
condition: motor vehicles

text: For trailers, the cumulative horizontal length of the side conspicuity marking elements, excluding any horizontal overlap, shall equate to at least 70 per cent of the overall length of the vehicle (excluding the drawbar).
condition: trailers

text: Line markings and contour markings lower element(s) shall be as low as practicable within the range of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.

A maximum mounting height of 2,500 mm for line markings and contour marking lower element(s) may be accepted only where the shape, structure, design or operational conditions of the vehicle prevent compliance with 1,500 mm or, if necessary, to fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 6.21.4.1.2. and 6.21.4.2.2. or the horizontal positioning of the line marking or lower element(s) of the contour marking.
condition: where compliance with 1,500 mm is prevented

text: The necessary justification for installation of conspicuity material higher than 1,500 mm shall be indicated in the communication form.
condition: if conspicuity material is installed higher than 1,500 mm

text: Contour markings upper element(s) shall be as high as practicable, but within 400 mm of the upper extremity of the vehicle.
condition: contour markings

text: At least 70 per cent of the illuminating surface of the installed conspicuity marking shall be visible when viewed by an observer positioned at any point within the defined observation planes.

For rear and front conspicuity markings, visibility shall be verified from an observation plane perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle situated 25 m from the extreme end of the vehicle, bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 3.0 m above the ground.
condition: rear and front conspicuity markings

text: For rear and front conspicuity markings, the observation plane shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes forming an angle of 4° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane and passing through the intersection of the vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width and the plane perpendicular to the longitudinal axis delimiting the end of the vehicle.
condition: rear and front conspicuity markings

text: For side conspicuity markings, visibility shall be verified from an observation plane parallel to the longitudinal median plane situated 25 m from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1.0 m and 1.5 m above the ground.
condition: side conspicuity markings

text: For side conspicuity markings, the observation plane shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes forming an angle of 4° outwards from a plane perpendicular to the vehicle's longitudinal axis and passing through the intersection of the vertical planes perpendicular to the longitudinal axis delimiting the vehicle's overall length and the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: side conspicuity markings

text: Side conspicuity markings shall be oriented as close as practicable to being parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operation requirements of the vehicle; if this is not possible, they shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
condition: side markings

text: Rear and front conspicuity markings shall be oriented as close as practicable to being parallel to the transverse plane of the vehicle, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operation requirements of the vehicle; if this is not possible, they shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
condition: rear and front markings

text: For conspicuity markings to be considered continuous, the distance between adjacent elements shall be as small as possible and shall not exceed 50 per cent of the shortest adjacent element length.

If the manufacturer proves to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that it is impossible to respect 50 per cent, the distance between adjacent conspicuity marking elements may be larger than 50 per cent of the shortest adjacent element but shall be as small as possible and not exceed 1,000 mm.
condition: if impossibility to respect 50 per cent is proven

text: In the case of a partial contour marking, each upper corner shall be described by two lines at 90° to each other, each at least 250 mm in length; if this is not possible, the marking shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
condition: partial contour marking

text: The distance between the conspicuity marking fitted to the rear of a vehicle and each mandatory stop lamp should be greater than 200 mm.
condition: rear conspicuity marking

text: Rear marking plates may be considered, at the discretion of the manufacturer, as part of the rear conspicuity marking for calculating its length and proximity to the side of the vehicle only if they are type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 70 or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
condition: where rear marking plates are installed

text: The locations on the vehicle designated for conspicuity markings shall allow for the installation of markings of at least 60 mm in width.
Where not otherwise specified in paragraph 6.22, the requirements for main-beam headlamps (paragraph 6.1.) and for dipped-beam headlamps (paragraph 6.2.) apply to the relevant part of the AFS.
The AFS is optional on motor vehicles.
The AFS is prohibited on trailers.
The number of AFS shall be one, type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
The AFS shall, prior to the position test procedures, be set to the neutral state.
