For a given lighting function or mode, the width and height requirements of paragraphs 6.22.4.1.1. to 6.22.4.1.4. shall be fulfilled by those AFS lighting units which are energized simultaneously for that lighting function or mode, according to the applicant's description, with all dimensions referring to the nearest edge of the apparent surface(s) observed in the direction of the reference axis of the lighting unit(s).

Two symmetrically placed AFS lighting units (one on each side of the vehicle, with the geometric centres of gravity of their apparent surfaces at the same height and at the same distance from the vehicle's longitudinal median plane within a tolerance of 50 mm each) shall be positioned at a height in compliance with the requirements of paragraphs 6.1.4. and 6.2.4.

Additional AFS lighting units, if any, on either side of the vehicle shall be positioned at a distance not exceeding 140 mm in horizontal direction (200 mm in case of additional two symmetrically placed lighting units) and 400 mm in vertical direction above or below from the nearest lighting unit.
condition: if additional lighting units are fitted

text: None of the additional AFS lighting units described in paragraph 6.22.4.1.2. shall be positioned lower than 250 mm above the ground.
condition: if additional lighting units are fitted

text: None of the additional AFS lighting units described in paragraph 6.22.4.1.2. shall be positioned higher above the ground than indicated in paragraph 6.2.4.2.
condition: if additional lighting units are fitted

text: For each mode of the AFS passing-beam lighting, the outer edge of the apparent surface of at least one lighting unit on each side of the vehicle shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For each mode of the AFS passing-beam lighting, the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm apart; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm. This does not apply to M1 and N1 category vehicles.

All lighting units of an AFS shall be mounted at the front; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.

On each side of the vehicle, for each AFS lighting function and mode provided, the angles of geometric visibility prescribed in paragraphs 6.1.5. and 6.2.5. shall be met by at least one of the lighting units simultaneously energized to perform that function and mode(s), according to the applicant's description; individual lighting units may be used to comply with the requirements for different angles.
The AFS shall be oriented towards the front.
The AFS shall, prior to the orientation test procedures, be set to the neutral state, emitting the basic passing-beam.

The initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the AFS basic passing-beam, set in the unladen vehicle state with one person in the driver's seat, shall be specified by the manufacturer within an accuracy of 0.1 per cent.

The initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the AFS basic passing-beam shall be indicated in a clearly legible and indelible manner on each vehicle, close to either the front lighting system or the manufacturer's plate, by the symbol shown in Annex 7.

Where differing initial downward inclinations are specified for different lighting units that provide or contribute to the cut-off of the basic passing-beam, these values shall be specified within an accuracy of 0.1 per cent and indicated in a clearly legible and indelible manner on each vehicle, close to either the relevant lighting units or on the manufacturer's plate, by the symbol shown in Annex 7, such that all lighting units concerned can be unambiguously identified.
condition: where differing initial downward inclinations are specified for different lighting units

text: The value(s) of the indicated initial downward inclination(s) of the AFS basic passing-beam shall be specified by the vehicle manufacturer within the range defined in paragraph 6.2.6.1.2. in relation to the mounting height of the lighting units that provide or contribute to the cut-off.

Different values of the initial downward inclination for different variants/versions of the same vehicle type may be specified within the range defined in paragraph 6.2.6.1.2., provided that only the pertinent value is indicated on each variant/version.
condition: if different values are specified for different variants/versions

text: The downward inclination of the horizontal part of the cut-off of the AFS basic passing-beam shall remain between the limits indicated in paragraph 6.2.6.1.2. under all the static loading conditions of the vehicle of Annex 5.

In case the passing-beam is generated by several beams from different AFS lighting units, the vertical inclination requirements apply to each beam's cut-off (if any) which is designed to project into the angular zone indicated in Annex 1 to UN Regulation No. 149.
condition: if the passing-beam is generated by several beams from different lighting units

text: Where a headlamp levelling device is necessary to satisfy the requirements of paragraph 6.22.6.1.2., the device shall be automatic.
condition: if a headlamp levelling device is necessary

text: In the event of a failure of the headlamp levelling device, the AFS basic passing beam shall not assume a position in which the vertical inclination is less downward than it was at the time when the failure occurred.
condition: in the event of failure of the levelling device

text: For each AFS lighting unit, the kink of the elbow of the cut-off line, if any, when projected on the screen, shall coincide with the vertical line through the reference axis of that lighting unit, with a tolerance of 0.5 degree to the side of the traffic direction.
condition: if the lighting unit has a cut-off with a kink

text: Other AFS lighting units shall be adjusted horizontally according to the applicant's specification, as defined according to Annex 14 to UN Regulation No. 149.

After adjustment of the initial setting of beam orientation, the vertical inclination of the AFS passing-beam or, when applicable, of all the different lighting units that provide or contribute to the cut-off(s) of the basic passing-beam, shall be verified for all loading conditions of the vehicle in accordance with paragraphs 6.2.6.3.1. and 6.2.6.3.2.

The AFS lighting units for the main-beam may be switched ON either simultaneously or in pairs; for changing over from the dipped-beam to the main-beam at least one pair of lighting units for the main-beam shall be switched ON.
condition: if main-beam is provided by the AFS

text: For changing over from the main-beam to the dipped-beam, all AFS lighting units for the main-beam shall be switched OFF simultaneously.
condition: if main-beam is provided by the AFS

text: The AFS main-beam may be designed to be adaptive, subject to paragraph 6.22.9.4., only with control signals produced by a sensor system capable of detecting and reacting to each of: (a) ambient lighting conditions; (b) the light emitted by the front lighting and front light-signalling devices of oncoming vehicles; (c) the light emitted by the rear light-signalling of preceding vehicles (vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, T and bicycles, equipped with retro-reflectors and lighting and light-signalling devices switched ON).
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: It shall always be possible to switch the AFS main-beam headlamps, adaptive or non-adaptive, ON and OFF manually and to manually deactivate the automatic control.
condition: if main-beam is provided by the AFS

text: The switching OFF of the AFS main-beam headlamps and the deactivation of their automatic control shall be by means of a simple and immediate manual operation; the use of sub-menus is not allowed.
condition: if main-beam is provided by the AFS

text: Where four concealable AFS lighting units are fitted, their raised position shall prevent the simultaneous operation of any additional headlamps fitted, if these are intended to provide light signals consisting of intermittent switching ON at short intervals in daylight.
condition: where four concealable lighting units are fitted and additional headlamps are intended for intermittent daylight signals

text: The control for changing over to the dipped-beam shall switch OFF all main-beam headlamps or switch OFF all AFS lighting units for the main-beam simultaneously.
In the case of AFS lighting units for the dipped-beam equipped with gas-discharge light sources, the gas-discharge light sources shall remain switched ON during the main-beam operation.
condition: if dipped-beam lighting units are equipped with gas-discharge light sources

text: The switching ON and OFF of the AFS dipped-beam shall fulfil the electrical connection requirements of paragraphs 5.12. and 6.2.7.

The changes within and between the provided classes and their modes of the AFS lighting functions shall be performed automatically without causing discomfort, distraction or glare, neither for the driver nor for other road users.
The class C mode(s) of the AFS passing-beam shall be activated if no mode of another passing-beam class is activated.

The class V mode(s) of the AFS passing-beam shall not operate unless one or more of the following is automatically detected (V-signal): (a) roads in built-up areas and vehicle speed not exceeding 60 km/h; (b) roads with fixed road illumination and vehicle speed not exceeding 60 km/h; (c) a road surface luminance of 1 cd/m2 and/or a horizontal road illumination of 10 lx being exceeded continuously; (d) vehicle speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
condition: if class V mode is provided

text: The class E mode(s) of the AFS passing-beam shall not operate unless the vehicle's speed exceeds 60 km/h and the road characteristics correspond to motorway conditions or the vehicle's speed exceeds 110 km/h (E-signal) is automatically detected.
condition: if class E mode is provided

text: For a Class E mode of the AFS passing beam complying with data set E1, the mode shall not operate unless the vehicle's speed exceeds 100 km/h (E1-signal).
condition: if Class E mode complies with data set E1

text: For a Class E mode of the AFS passing beam complying with data set E2, the mode shall not operate unless the vehicle's speed exceeds 90 km/h (E2-signal).
condition: if Class E mode complies with data set E2

text: For a Class E mode of the AFS passing beam complying with data set E3, the mode shall not operate unless the vehicle's speed exceeds 80 km/h (E3-signal).
condition: if Class E mode complies with data set E3

text: The class W mode(s) of the AFS passing-beam shall not operate unless the front fog lamps, if any, are switched OFF and one or more of the following is automatically detected (W-signal): (a) wetness of the road detected automatically; (b) the windshield wiper is operating and its continuous or automatically controlled operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes.
condition: if class W mode is provided

text: A mode of a class C, V, E or W AFS passing-beam shall not be modified to become a bending mode (T-signal) unless at least one of the following (or equivalent indications) is evaluated: (a) the angle of lock of the steering; (b) the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle.
condition: if a bending mode is provided

text: A horizontal movement of the asymmetric cut-off side-wards from the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, if any, is allowed only when the vehicle is in forward motion (not applicable when bend lighting is produced for a right turn in right-hand traffic or left turn in left-hand traffic).
condition: if the asymmetric cut-off is moved horizontally

text: A horizontal movement of the asymmetric cut-off shall be such that the longitudinal vertical plane through the kink of the elbow of the cut-off does not intersect the line of the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle at distances from the front of the vehicle larger than 100 times the mounting height of the respective lighting unit.
condition: if the asymmetric cut-off is moved horizontally

text: One or more AFS lighting units may be additionally energized for bending mode only when the horizontal radius of curvature of the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle is 500 m or less.
condition: if additional lighting units are energized for bending mode

text: It shall always be possible for the driver to set the AFS to the neutral state and to return it to its automatic operation.
The tell-tale provisions of paragraph 6.1.8. (main-beam headlamp) and 6.2.8. (dipped-beam headlamp) apply to the respective parts of an AFS.
A visual failure tell-tale for AFS is mandatory and shall be non-flashing.

The AFS failure tell-tale shall be activated whenever a failure is detected with respect to the AFS control signals or when a failure signal is received in accordance with paragraph 4.13. of UN Regulation No. 149, and shall remain activated while the failure is present.
The AFS failure tell-tale may be cancelled temporarily, but shall be repeated whenever the device which starts and stops the propulsion system is switched ON and OFF.

If the main-beam is adaptive, a visual tell-tale shall be provided to indicate to the driver that the adaptation of the main beam is activated, and this information shall remain displayed as long as the adaptation is activated.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: An AFS shall be permitted only in conjunction with the installation of headlamp cleaning device(s) according to UN Regulation No. 45 for at least those lighting units indicated under item 9.2.2.3. of the communication form of UN Regulation No. 149 which contribute to the Class C (basic) passing beam, if the total objective luminous flux of the light source(s) and/or light source module(s) of these units exceeds 2,000 lm at least on one side.
condition: if total objective luminous flux of units contributing to Class C passing beam exceeds 2,000 lm on at least one side

text: Lighting units for AFS passing beam and/or adaptive main beam may produce Driver Assistance Projection only in order to warn the driver appropriately regarding special traffic situations or conditions.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is produced

text: The applicant shall demonstrate with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority the correspondence of the AFS control signals to the description required in paragraph 3.2.6. and to the respective AFS control signals specified in the AFS type approval documents.

The applicant shall demonstrate with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority compliance with the AFS automatic operating requirements of paragraphs 6.22.7.4.1. through 6.22.7.4.5.

The applicant shall demonstrate with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority compliance of Driver Assistance Projection, if any, with paragraph 5.35. and its sub-paragraphs.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is provided

text: To verify that the AFS automatic operation of the passing-beam functions does not cause any discomfort, the technical service shall perform a test drive comprising any situation relevant to the system control on the basis of the applicant's description, noting whether all modes are activated, performing and de-activated according to the description; obvious malfunctioning (e.g. excessive angular movement or flicker) shall be contested.
If Driver Assistance Projection is present, the technical service shall verify during the test drive that this feature does not cause any distraction.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is present

text: The overall performance of the AFS automatic control, including Driver Assistance Projection if installed, shall be demonstrated by the applicant by documentation or by other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.

The manufacturer shall provide a documentation package giving access to the design of the safety concept of the AFS, describing the measures designed into the system to address system integrity and ensure safe operation even in the event of mechanical or electrical failure which could cause discomfort, distraction or glare to the driver or to oncoming and preceding vehicles.

The AFS safety concept documentation shall give a simple explanation of all the control functions of the system and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised, and shall explain the functions of the system and the safety concept as laid down by the manufacturer.
A list of all input and sensed variables of the AFS shall be provided and their working range shall be defined.
The possibility of a fall-back to the basic passing-beam (class C) function shall be a part of the AFS safety concept.
The AFS documentation shall be brief, yet provide evidence that the design and development has had the benefit of expertise from all the system fields involved.
For periodic technical inspections, the AFS documentation shall describe how the current operational status of the system can be checked.
For type approval purposes the AFS documentation shall be taken as the basic reference for the verification process.

To verify that the adaptation of the main beam, including Driver Assistance Projection, does not cause any discomfort, distraction or glare to the driver or to oncoming and preceding vehicles, the technical service shall perform a test drive according to paragraph 2 of Annex 12, including any situation relevant to the system control on the basis of the applicant's description.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: The performance of the adaptation of the main beam shall be documented and checked against the applicant's description; any obvious malfunctioning (e.g. excessive angular movement or flicker) shall be contested.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: The boundaries of the minimum fields in which the adaptive main-beam sensor is able to detect light emitted from other vehicles shall be given by the angles indicated in paragraph 6.1.9.3.1.1.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: The adaptive main-beam sensor system sensitivity shall comply with the requirements in paragraph 6.1.9.3.1.2.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: The adaptive main-beam shall be switched OFF when the illuminance produced by ambient lighting conditions exceeds 7,000 lx.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: Compliance with the 7,000 lx switch-OFF requirement of the adaptive main-beam shall be demonstrated by the applicant using simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Type Approval Authority; if necessary the illuminance shall be measured on a horizontal surface with a cosine corrected sensor at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle.
condition: if the main-beam is adaptive

text: The reference value corresponding to an aggregate maximum intensity of the AFS lighting units that can be energized simultaneously to provide the main-beam lighting or its modes shall not exceed 100, obtained by adding together the individual reference marks indicated on the installation units simultaneously used to provide the main beam.
condition: if main-beam is provided by the AFS

text: The means according to paragraph 4.12. of UN Regulation No. 149, which allow the vehicle to be used temporarily in a territory with the opposite direction of driving, shall be explained in detail in the owner's manual.
The emergency stop signal shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
The number of lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.2. or 6.7.2.
The arrangement of the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.3. or 6.7.3.
The position of the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4. or 6.7.4.
The geometric visibility of the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.5. or 6.7.5.
The orientation of the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.6. or 6.7.6.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
If any of the lamps of the emergency stop signal to the rear of the vehicle use filament light sources the frequency shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz.
condition: if any rear lamp of the emergency stop signal uses filament light sources

text: The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the hazard warning signal is activated.

If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer, the control of the emergency stop signal on the motor vehicle shall also be capable of operating the emergency stop signal on the trailer, except as provided in paragraph 6.23.9.2.
condition: if the motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer

text: When the motor vehicle is electrically connected to a trailer, the operating frequency of the emergency stop signal for the combination shall be limited to 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz (paragraph 6.23.7.1.1.); however, if the motor vehicle can detect that filament light sources are not being used on the trailer for the emergency stop signal, the frequency may be 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz (paragraph 6.23.7.1.).
condition: when the motor vehicle is electrically connected to a trailer

text: If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer fitted with a service braking system of either continuous or semi-continuous type, as defined in Regulation No. 13, it shall be ensured that a constant power supply is provided via the electrical connector for the stop lamps to such trailers while the service brake is applied; the emergency stop signal on any such trailer may operate independently of the towing vehicle and is not required to operate at the same frequency as, or in phase with that on the towing vehicle.
condition: if the motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer with continuous or semi-continuous service braking system

text: The number of exterior courtesy lamps shall be one or two; further exterior courtesy lamps to illuminate steps and/or door handles, and/or the area around the vehicle are permitted.
Each door handle or step shall be illuminated by not more than one exterior courtesy lamp.
The arrangement of exterior courtesy lamps shall meet the requirements of paragraph 6.24.9.3.

The exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall not be switched ON unless the vehicle is stationary and one or more of the following conditions is satisfied: (a) the propulsion system is stopped; or (b) a driver or passenger door is opened or after being closed; or (c) a load compartment door is opened or after being closed.
The exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall be switched OFF when the vehicle is no longer stationary.
Where the exterior courtesy lamp(s) vary in luminous intensity and/or apparent surface, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
condition: if the exterior courtesy lamp varies in luminous intensity or apparent surface

text: The exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall not flash.

Only approved lamps emitting white light, with the exception of main-beam headlamps, daytime running lamps and reversing lamps, may be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamp(s); in addition, rear position lamps, parking lamps, side-marker lamps and/or end-outline marker lamps may be switched ON.
condition: if other lamps are used as exterior courtesy lamps

text: The Technical Service shall perform a visual test to verify that there is no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the exterior courtesy lamps if viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone on a transverse plane 10 m from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear of the vehicle, and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these four planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above and perpendicular to the ground as shown in Annex 14.

condition: at the request of the applicant and with the consent of the Technical Service

text: The rear-end collision alert signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.25.7.

text: The number of lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.2.
The arrangement of lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.3.
The position of lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.
The geometric visibility of lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.5.
The orientation of lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.6.

Compliance with the electrical connection requirements of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be demonstrated by the applicant, by simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Technical Service responsible for type approval.
All the lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 +/- 1.0 Hz.
If any of the lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal to the rear of the vehicle use filament light sources the frequency shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz.
condition: if any rear lamp of the signal uses filament light sources

text: The rear-end collision alert signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall not be switched ON if the direction-indicator lamps, the hazard warning signal or the emergency stop signal is activated.

The rear-end collision alert signal may only be switched ON when Vr > 30 km/h and TTC ≤ 1.4, or when Vr ≤ 30 km/h and TTC ≤ 1.4 / 30 × Vr, where Vr is the relative speed to the following vehicle in the same lane and TTC is the time to collision.
The switch ON period of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be not more than 3 seconds.
Side mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be one or two (one per side) on vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length.
condition: vehicle length not exceeding 6 m

text: Side mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be a maximum of four (up to two per side) on vehicles above 6 m and up to and including 9 m in length.
condition: vehicle length above 6 m up to and including 9 m

text: Side mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be a maximum of six (up to three per side) on vehicles exceeding 9 m in length.
condition: vehicle length exceeding 9 m

condition: rear mounted

text: Installed manoeuvring lamps (mounted to the side or rear) shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The arrangement of manoeuvring lamps shall meet the requirements of paragraph 6.26.9.
Side mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
condition: side mounted

text: Rear mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be no higher than the vehicle.
condition: rear mounted

text: In the case of the installation of more than one side mounted manoeuvring lamp, the lamps shall be mounted as symmetrically as practicable along each side of the vehicle.
condition: more than one side mounted lamp

text: The distance between two adjacent side mounted manoeuvring lamps on the same side shall not be less than 0.5 m.
condition: side mounted

text: Rear mounted manoeuvring lamps shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
condition: rear mounted

text: Manoeuvring lamps shall be oriented downwards, and the requirements of paragraph 6.26.9. apply.

On motor vehicles, manoeuvring lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be switched ON unless the main-beam headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps of the motor vehicle are switched ON at the same time.

On motor vehicles, the manoeuvring lamp(s) shall be switched ON automatically for slow manoeuvres up to 15 km/h provided that one of the following conditions is fulfilled: (a) prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the propulsion system; or (b) reverse gear is engaged; or (c) a camera-based system which assists parking manoeuvres is operating.

On motor vehicles, the manoeuvring lamps shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h and they shall remain switched OFF until the switch ON conditions are met again.

On trailers, manoeuvring lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be activated unless the position lamps of the trailer are switched ON at the same time and shall take their input speed directly from the trailer.

On trailers, the manoeuvring lamp(s) shall be switched ON automatically for slow manoeuvres up to 15 km/h provided that one of the following conditions is fulfilled: (a) prior to the trailer being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the vehicle propulsion system; or (b) the reverse lamp is switched ON; or (c) a camera-based system which assists parking manoeuvres is operating.

On trailers, the manoeuvring lamps shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the trailer exceeds 15 km/h and they shall remain switched OFF until the switch ON conditions are met again.

The Technical Service shall perform a visual test to verify that there is no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the manoeuvring lamps if viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone on a transverse plane 10 m from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear of the vehicle, and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these four planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above and parallel to the ground as shown in Annex 14.

condition: at the request of the applicant and with the consent of the Technical Service

The arrangement of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The position in width of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.
The position in height of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.
The position in length of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.

The geometric visibility of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used, but may be reduced in comparison to them.
The orientation of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.
The answer-back signal shall only operate under the park condition of a vehicle.
If the answer-back signal flashes, the frequency shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.
condition: if the answer-back signal flashes

text: The answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices and exterior courtesy lamps whose maximum luminous intensity per lamp does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
Front fog lamps, rear fog lamps and stop lamps shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.
The answer-back signal may only be activated automatically in conjunction with the locking and unlocking of the door(s) and/or the detection of the vehicle user in proximity to the vehicle.

The duration of the optical indication of the answer-back signal, from the beginning to the end of the signal irrespective of flashes, intensity variations or apparent surface variations, shall not exceed 3 seconds.

condition: if fitted

The position of reversing projectors shall be such that the provisions of paragraphs 6.28.5., 6.28.6. and 6.28.9. are fulfilled.
The lateral distance from the outer edge of the reversing projection with respect to the longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall not be more than 1,875 mm.
The longitudinal distance from the farthest edge of the reversing projection shall not be more than 3,000 mm from the backward extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The patterns of the reversing projections shall start with their closest edge within a rectangle, symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane and adjacent to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, with a width of 1,000 mm and a length of 3,750 mm.

condition: if provided

text: The Technical Service shall perform a visual test to verify that there is no direct visibility of the apparent surface of any reversing projector if viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone on a transverse plane 10 m from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear of the vehicle, and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these four planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above and perpendicular to the ground as shown in Annex 14; this is deemed satisfied if the installation conditions comply with paragraph 5.12.1.2. (a) in the 01 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, and may also be verified by drawing or simulation at the request of the applicant and with the consent of the Technical Service.

condition: if paragraph 6.28.9.1. is not fulfilled

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the Agreement, Appendix 2 (E/ECE/324-E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.2), with the requirements of paragraphs 8.1 to 8.4.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6.

The holder of the approval shall ensure existence of procedures for effective quality control of the vehicle as regards all aspects relevant to compliance with the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6.
The holder of the approval shall ensure that for each type of vehicle at least the tests prescribed in Annex 9 or physical checks from which equivalent data may be derived are carried out.
Tests carried out by the Type Approval Authority shall be on samples selected at random without causing distortion of the manufacturer's delivery commitments.
The Type Approval Authority shall strive to obtain a frequency of inspection of once per year, at its discretion.
In the case where negative results are recorded, the Type Approval Authority shall ensure that all necessary steps are taken to re-establish the conformity of production as rapidly as possible.
condition: where negative results are recorded

The approval mark affixed to the vehicle (Model B, according to paragraph 4.5., combined with approvals under other Regulations) shall have a dimension a of not less than 8 mm.
condition: if the vehicle is approved under one or more other Regulations and the marks are arranged according to paragraph 4.5.

text: Where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and the apparent surface 7b is based on the light-emitting surface according to paragraph 2.10.2., function F1 shall not be transparent to function F2 for the two functions to be assessed as in the example for reciprocal incorporation.
condition: in the case where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and 7b is the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2.

text: For verifying the visibility of red light to the front and white light to the rear (paragraph 5.10.4.), Zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

For verifying the visibility of red light to the front and white light to the rear (paragraph 5.10.4.), Zones 1 and 2 shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.
For the loading tests determining variations in the vertical orientation of the dipped-beam headlamps, the mass of the passengers shall be calculated on the basis of 75 kg per person.
For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: one person in the driver's seat.
For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: the driver, plus one passenger in the front seat farthest from the driver.

For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: the driver, one passenger in the front seat farthest from the driver, all the seats farthest to the rear occupied.
For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: all the seats occupied.

For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: all the seats occupied, plus an evenly distributed load in the luggage boot in order to obtain the permissible load on the rear axle (or on the front axle if the boot is at the front); if the vehicle has a front and a rear boot, the additional load shall be appropriately distributed to obtain the permissible axle loads; if the maximum permissible laden mass is obtained before the permissible load on one of the axles, the loading of the boot(s) shall be limited to the figure which enables that mass to be reached.

For M1 vehicles, the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load condition: driver, plus an evenly distributed load in the boot in order to obtain the permissible load on the corresponding axle; if the maximum permissible laden mass is obtained before the permissible load on the axle, the loading of the boot(s) shall be limited to the figure which enables that mass to be reached.
For M1 vehicles, in determining the loading conditions for the dipped-beam inclination, account shall be taken of any loading restrictions laid down by the manufacturer.
For M2 and M3 vehicles, the angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the loading condition: vehicle unladen and one person in the driver's seat.

For M2 and M3 vehicles, the angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the loading condition: vehicle laden such that each axle carries its maximum technically permissible load or until the maximum permissible mass of the vehicle is attained by loading the front and rear axles proportionally to their maximum technically permissible loads, whichever occurs first.

For N category vehicles with load surfaces, the angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the loading condition: vehicle unladen and one person in the driver's seat.
condition: vehicles with load surfaces

text: For N category vehicles with load surfaces, the angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the loading condition: driver, plus a load so distributed as to give the maximum technically permissible load on the rear axle or axles, or the maximum permissible mass of the vehicle, whichever occurs first, without exceeding a front axle load calculated as the sum of the front axle load of the unladen vehicle plus 25 per cent of the maximum permissible payload on the front axle (conversely for the front axle when the load platform is at the front).
condition: vehicles with load surfaces

text: For N category drawing vehicles for semi-trailers without a load surface, the angle of the dipped beam shall be determined under the loading condition: unladen vehicle without a load on the coupling attachment and one person in the driver's seat.
condition: drawing vehicles for semi-trailers without a load surface

text: For N category drawing vehicles for semi-trailers without a load surface, the angle of the dipped beam shall be determined under the loading condition: one person in the driver's seat and the technically permissible load on the coupling attachment in the position of the attachment corresponding to the highest load on the rear axle.
condition: drawing vehicles for semi-trailers without a load surface

text: For N category drawing vehicles for trailers without a load surface, the angle of the dipped beam shall be determined under the loading condition: vehicle unladen and one person in the driver's seat.
condition: drawing vehicles for trailers without a load surface

text: For N category drawing vehicles for trailers without a load surface, the angle of the dipped beam shall be determined under the loading condition: one person in the driver's seat, all the other places in the driving cabin being occupied.
condition: drawing vehicles for trailers without a load surface

text: If a visual inspection of the dipped-beam pattern on the screen or a photometric method is used, the measurement of dipped-beam inclination shall be carried out in a dark environment (e.g. a dark room) of sufficient area to allow the vehicle and the screen to be placed as shown in Figure 1.
condition: if a visual inspection on the screen or a photometric method is used

text: Headlamp centres of reference shall be at a distance from the screen of at least 10 m.
condition: if a visual inspection on the screen or a photometric method is used

text: The ground on which dipped-beam inclination measurements are made shall be as flat and horizontal as possible, so that the reproducibility of measurements of dipped-beam inclination can be assured with an accuracy of ±0.5 mrad (±0.05 per cent inclination).

If a screen is used, its marking, position and orientation in relation to the ground and to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall be such that the reproducibility of the measurement of the dipped-beam inclination can be assured with an accuracy of ±0.5 mrad (±0.05 per cent inclination).
condition: if a screen is used

text: During dipped-beam inclination measurements, the ambient temperature shall be between 10 and 30 °C.
Dipped-beam inclination measurements shall be carried out on a vehicle which has travelled a distance of between 1,000 km and 10,000 km, preferably 5,000 km.
For dipped-beam inclination measurements, the tyres shall be inflated to the full-load pressure specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

For dipped-beam inclination measurements, the vehicle shall be fully replenished (fuel, water, oil), with the fuel tank filled to not less than 90 per cent of its capacity, and equipped with all the accessories and tools specified by the manufacturer.
For dipped-beam inclination measurements, the vehicle shall have the parking brake released and the gearbox in neutral.
For dipped-beam inclination measurements, the vehicle shall be conditioned for at least 8 h at an ambient temperature between 10 and 30 °C.

If a photometric or visual method is used, headlamps with a well-defined dipped-beam cut-off should preferably be installed on the vehicle under test to facilitate the measurements; other means are allowed to obtain a more precise reading (e.g. removal of the headlamp lens).
condition: if a photometric or visual method is used

text: The variations in either dipped-beam or vehicle inclination, depending on the method chosen, shall be measured separately for each side of the vehicle.
The results obtained from both left and right dipped-beam headlamps under all the load conditions specified in Annex 5 shall be within the limits set out in Annex 6 paragraph 5.5.
During the dipped-beam inclination measurement the load shall be applied gradually without subjecting the vehicle to excessive shocks.
Where an AFS is fitted, the dipped-beam inclination measurements shall be carried out with the AFS in its neutral state.
condition: where an AFS is fitted

text: For determination of the measured initial inclination, the vehicle shall be prepared as specified in Annex 6 paragraph 4 and laden as specified in Annex 5 (first loading condition of the respective vehicle category).
Before each measurement of the initial inclination, the vehicle shall be rocked as specified in Annex 6 paragraph 5.4, and measurements shall be made three times.
If none of the three measured initial inclination results differ by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination) from the arithmetic mean of the results, that mean shall constitute the final result.
condition: if no result differs by more than 2 mrad from the mean

text: If any initial inclination measurement differs from the arithmetic mean of the results by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination), a further series of 10 measurements shall be made, the arithmetic mean of which shall constitute the final result.
condition: if any measurement differs by more than 2 mrad from the mean

text: Any method may be used to measure variations of dipped-beam inclination provided that the readings are accurate to within ±0.2 mrad (±0.02 per cent inclination).

In each loading condition, the vehicle suspension and any other part likely to affect dipped-beam inclination shall be activated according to the methods described in Annex 6 paragraph 5.4; other methods (experimental or based upon calculations) may be jointly proposed by the technical authorities and manufacturers provided such calculations are clearly valid.

For M1 vehicles with conventional suspension, with the vehicle on the measuring site (with wheels on floating platforms if their absence would restrict suspension movement likely to affect the results), the vehicle shall be rocked continuously for at least three complete cycles, each cycle pushing down first the rear and then the front end, the sequence ending with the completion of a cycle; alternatively the vehicle may be moved backwards and forwards for at least a complete wheel revolution instead of using floating platforms.
condition: conventional suspension

text: Before making the measurements, the M1 vehicle shall be allowed to come to rest spontaneously.
condition: conventional suspension

text: For M2, M3 and N vehicles with conventional suspension, if the M1 treatment method of paragraph 5.4.1 is not possible, the method of paragraph 5.4.2.2 or 5.4.2.3 may be used.
condition: conventional suspension and M1 method not possible

text: For M2, M3 and N vehicles with conventional suspension, with the vehicle on the measuring site and wheels on the ground, the vehicle shall be rocked by temporarily varying the load.
condition: if this method is chosen

text: For M2, M3 and N vehicles with conventional suspension, with the vehicle on the measuring site and wheels on the ground, the vehicle suspension and all other parts which may affect the dipped-beam inclination shall be activated by using a vibration rig (e.g. a vibrating platform on which the wheels rest).
condition: if this method is chosen

text: For vehicles with non-conventional suspension where the propulsion system has to be running, before making any measurement the vehicle shall be allowed to assume its final attitude with the engine running.
condition: non-conventional suspension requiring propulsion system running

text: The variation of the inclination of the dipped beam shall be assessed for each of the different loading conditions in relation to the measured initial inclination determined in accordance with Annex 6 paragraph 5.2.

If the vehicle is fitted with a manual headlamp-levelling system, it shall be adjusted to the positions specified by the manufacturer for the given loading conditions (according to Annex 5) during the measurements.
condition: if a manual headlamp-levelling system is fitted

text: A single measurement shall first be made in each loading condition; requirements are met if, for all loading conditions, the variation in inclination is within the calculated limits (difference between the stated initial inclination and the lower and upper limits specified for approval) with a safety margin of 4 mrad (0.4 per cent inclination).

If the result of any measurement does not lie within the 4 mrad safety margin or exceeds the limit values, a further three measurements shall be made in the corresponding loading conditions as specified in Annex 6 paragraph 5.5.3.
condition: if a result is outside the safety margin or exceeds the limits

text: For each repeated loading condition, if none of the three measured results differs by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination) from the arithmetic mean, that mean shall constitute the final result.
condition: if no result differs by more than 2 mrad from the mean

text: For each repeated loading condition, if any measurement differs from the arithmetic mean by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination), a further series of 10 measurements shall be made, the arithmetic mean of which shall constitute the final result.
condition: if any measurement differs by more than 2 mrad from the mean

text: If the vehicle is fitted with an automatic headlamp-levelling system with an inherent hysteresis loop, average results at the top and bottom of the hysteresis loop shall be taken as significant values, all measurements being made in accordance with paragraphs 5.5.3.1 and 5.5.3.2.
condition: automatic headlamp-levelling system with inherent hysteresis loop

text: Requirements are met if, under all loading conditions, the variation between the measured initial inclination and the inclination measured under each loading condition is less than the values calculated in Annex 6 paragraph 5.5.1 (without safety margin).

If only one of the calculated upper or lower limits of variation is exceeded, the manufacturer may choose a different value for the stated initial inclination, within the limits specified for approval.
condition: if only one of the calculated limits is exceeded

text: The indication of the initial downward inclination of the dipped-beam headlamp cut-off and of the front fog lamp cut-off shall use the symbol shown in Annex 7; the size of the symbol and characters is left to the discretion of the manufacturer.

Inclination of the dipped beam by a manually adjusted headlamp-levelling device shall in all cases be produced by a simple control, the operation of which is clearly described in the owner's handbook.
condition: manually adjusted headlamp-levelling device per paragraph 6.2.6.2.2

text: The headlamp-levelling control shall carry symbol(s) indicating clearly the movements corresponding to the downward and upward inclination of the dipped beam.
condition: manually adjusted headlamp-levelling device

text: The "0" position of the headlamp-levelling control shall correspond to the initial inclination according to paragraph 6.2.6.1.1.
condition: manually adjusted headlamp-levelling device

text: The "0" position of the headlamp-levelling control shall be a "stop position", which need not necessarily be at the end of the scale.
condition: manually adjusted headlamp-levelling device

text: In conformity of production, the position of lamps in width, height and length shall be checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2, 2.10.3, 2.10.4, 2.3.3 and 5.4, and the measured distances shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

In conformity of production, the angles of geometric visibility shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7, and the measured angles shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the angle limits may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° mounting variation permitted in paragraph 5.3 for light-signalling devices.
In conformity of production, the visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.

In conformity of production, the initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the dipped beam and the front fog lamps shall be set to the plated figure shown per Annex 7, or alternatively to a different figure where it can be shown to be representative of the type approved when tested in accordance with Annex 6, in particular paragraph 4.1.

In conformity of production, the variation of the dipped-beam downward inclination as a function of the specified loading conditions shall remain within: for 0.5 ≤ h ≤ 0.9 m, upper limit -0.50 per cent and lower limit -(h + 1.2) per cent; for 0.9 < h ≤ 1.2 m (and 1.2 < h ≤ 1.5 m), upper limit -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) per cent and lower limit -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent.

In conformity of production, for a front fog lamp with light source(s) having a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens, the variation of the downward inclination with load shall remain within 0.7 per cent minimum and 3.3 per cent maximum vertical inclination for h < 0.8, and 1.2 per cent minimum and 3.8 per cent maximum vertical inclination for h > 0.8.

text: In conformity of production, the electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle, and the lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: The test course for the automatic main-beam control shall include test section B: combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations, in a frequency so that the main beam will switch ON and OFF, on multi-lane roads and country roads.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: The test course for the automatic main-beam control shall include test section C: active and passive overtaking manoeuvres, in a frequency so that the main beam will switch ON and OFF, on multi-lane roads and country roads.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: The test course for the automatic main-beam control shall include test section D: oncoming bicycle as described in paragraph 6.1.9.3.1.2, on country roads.

text: The test course for the automatic main-beam control shall include test section E: combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations in urban areas.

text: Urban areas of the automatic main-beam test drive shall comprise roads with and without illumination.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: Country roads of the automatic main-beam test drive shall comprise sections having two lanes and sections having four or more lanes and shall include junctions, hills and/or slopes, dips and winding roads.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: Multi-lane roads and country roads of the automatic main-beam test drive shall comprise sections having straight level parts with a length of more than 600 m and sections having curves to the left and to the right.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: Dense traffic situations shall be taken into account in the automatic main-beam test drive.
condition: automatic control of main-beam headlamps

text: The test drive for adaptive main-beam headlamps shall be carried out in clear atmosphere (meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m) and with clean headlamps.

The test course for the adaptive main beam shall comprise urban areas at 50 ± 10 km/h (10 per cent of course length), multi-lane roads at 100 ± 20 km/h (20 per cent) and country roads at 80 ± 20 km/h (70 per cent).

The test course for the adaptive main beam shall include test section A: single oncoming or single preceding vehicle, in a frequency so that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process, on multi-lane roads and country roads.

The test course for the adaptive main beam shall include test section B: combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations, in a frequency so that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process, on multi-lane roads and country roads.

The test course for the adaptive main beam shall include test section C: active and passive overtaking manoeuvres, in a frequency so that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process, on multi-lane roads and country roads.
The test course for the adaptive main beam shall include test section D: oncoming bicycle as described in paragraph 6.22.9.3.1.2, on country roads.
The test course for the adaptive main beam shall include test section E: combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations in urban areas.
Urban areas of the adaptive main-beam test drive shall comprise roads with and without illumination.

Country roads of the adaptive main-beam test drive shall comprise sections having two lanes and sections having four or more lanes and shall include junctions, hills and/or slopes, dips and winding roads.

Multi-lane roads and country roads of the adaptive main-beam test drive shall comprise sections having straight level parts with a length of more than 600 m and sections having curves to the left and to the right.
Dense traffic situations shall be taken into account in the adaptive main-beam test drive.

For test sections A and B, the test engineers shall evaluate and record the acceptability of the adaptation process of the adaptive main beam in relation to oncoming and preceding road users, being seated in the vehicle tested and additionally in the oncoming and preceding vehicles.
For test sections A, B, C and E, the test engineers shall evaluate the Driver Assistance Projection, if installed.
condition: if Driver Assistance Projection is installed

text: With ambient light outside the vehicle less than 1,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched ON automatically with a response time of no more than 2 seconds.
condition: ambient light less than 1,000 lux

text: With ambient light outside the vehicle between 1,000 lux and 7,000 lux, the switching state and response time of the dipped-beam headlamps are at the manufacturer's discretion.
condition: ambient light between 1,000 and 7,000 lux

text: With ambient light outside the vehicle more than 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched OFF automatically with a response time of more than 5 seconds but no more than 300 seconds.
condition: ambient light more than 7,000 lux

text: Compliance with the automatic dipped-beam switching conditions shall be demonstrated by the applicant, by simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Type Approval Authority.

The ambient illuminance for automatic dipped-beam switching shall be measured on a horizontal surface with a cosine corrected sensor at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle; this may be demonstrated by sufficient documentation or other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.

The direct visibility of the apparent surface of manoeuvring lamps, exterior courtesy lamps and reversing projectors shall be assessed from the zones of observation at the front, rear and both sides of the vehicle as shown in Annex 14.
Photometric measurements specified by angular coordinates shall use the gonio(photo)meter system shown in Annex 15 as defined in paragraph 2.10.9.
condition: if not otherwise specified

text: Driver Assistance Projection shall use only the symbols and patterns of Annex 16: slippery road warning, risk of collision warning, wrong way warning, lane keeping assist warning and predicted trajectory.

The risk of collision warning Driver Assistance Projection shall be triggered only when the relative speed is larger than 30 km/h and the Risk of Collision Time is less than 1.4 s; flashing at 4.0 Hz ± 1.0 Hz is allowed.
condition: risk of collision warning

text: The wrong way warning Driver Assistance Projection shall be activated only when the vehicle is entering a one-way road or a highway in opposite direction; flashing at 4.0 Hz ± 1.0 Hz is allowed.
condition: wrong way warning

text: The lane keeping assist warning Driver Assistance Projection shall be activated only if the vehicle unintentionally exits its lane.
condition: lane keeping assist warning

text: The predicted trajectory Driver Assistance Projection shall have the basic quadrilateral shape shown in Annex 16, which may change only when adapted in conformity with paragraph 5.35.12.
condition: predicted trajectory

text: The basic element used for reversing projection patterns shall be a rectangle; minor deviations from this shape when projected on the road due to technical restrictions or environmental conditions are considered to comply.
The colour of the basic element of the reversing projection shall be white.
